title: Triage a Literature Set Without Losing Its Limits
trigger: A person supplies papers or requests a bounded literature map.
not_for: Treating a popularity signal, search snippet or confident summary as sufficient evidence for a factual conclusion.
inputs: The research question and inclusion criteria
Papers or permitted search sources
steps: Freeze the question, eligible populations, designs, outcomes and date boundaries from the user or supplied protocol.
Normalize bibliographic identities conservatively, retaining original titles and identifiers; do not merge distinct studies because titles resemble one another.
Separate exact duplicates from companion reports of the same underlying study, with an explicit reason for each relation.
Screen title and abstract for obvious exclusions, then inspect accessible full text for the decisive criteria. Record unknown criteria explicitly.
Extract effect definitions, sample, follow-up and design limitations only from inspected material; do not pool incompatible measures.
Synthesize relevant independent study families, contradictions and gaps. State whether screening was single-reviewer and what remains unreviewed.
outputs: A reading order driven by unresolved questions

Return record dispositions, study-family groupings, eligibility reasons, access limitations and a bounded synthesis by question. Keep inaccessible full text unresolved rather than excluded for an invented methodological reason. Report search coverage accurately; a supplied-paper triage is not a systematic review of the whole literature.
checks: Duplicate cohorts are not counted as independent replication.
Missing methods remain unknown.
Study limitations survive the summary.
The task-specific structured output is checked against source facts or disclosed adjudication, while semantic usefulness still requires human review.
recovery: Preserve the protocol version, original record IDs, dedup and study-family map, exact screening reasons, access flags and extracted locators. Resume unresolved full-text decisions without rescreening settled records.
example: Compare these eight papers and identify which three are most useful for understanding the disagreement.
improvement: Add explicit record/report/study-family accounting and an unresolved-access state that can be checked on concrete inputs.

depth.domain_method: Triage distinguishes records, reports and underlying studies. Deduplicate bibliographic copies before screening, then group multiple reports of one study before interpreting replication. Apply prespecified eligibility in two stages and retain exclusion reasons. Evaluate methodological relevance and risk of bias separately from publication prestige; a count of favorable abstracts is not evidence synthesis.
depth.output_contract: Return record dispositions, study-family groupings, eligibility reasons, access limitations and a bounded synthesis by question. Keep inaccessible full text unresolved rather than excluded for an invented methodological reason. Report search coverage accurately; a supplied-paper triage is not a systematic review of the whole literature.

decisions.when: Two records share a DOI but differ in downloaded filename.
decisions.do: Treat them as one bibliographic record and retain both source locations.
decisions.avoid: Do not count two downloads as two independent studies.

decisions.when: Two papers report different follow-ups from the same cohort.
decisions.do: Group them into one study family while retaining the distinct time points and outcomes.
decisions.avoid: Do not discard the later report or count it as independent replication.

decisions.when: An eligibility criterion requires unavailable full text.
decisions.do: Mark the report awaiting full-text review with the exact missing criterion.
decisions.avoid: Do not infer inclusion or methodological exclusion from a missing PDF.

decisions.when: A study reports an incompatible outcome scale.
decisions.do: Keep a narrative comparison or a justified conversion with the original units intact.
decisions.avoid: Do not average raw scores with different meanings.

decisions.when: The task is a rapid map of supplied papers.
decisions.do: Bound the claim to that corpus and state the single-screening limitation.
decisions.avoid: Do not label the result exhaustive or PRISMA-complete merely because a flow table exists.

failure_modes.symptom: The synthesis claims many replications from one cohort.
failure_modes.cause: Reports were counted instead of independent study families.
failure_modes.repair: Reconstruct the family map from recruitment, registry and author-described cohort links.
failure_modes.recheck: Independent counts use families, and report-level outcomes remain traceable.

failure_modes.symptom: Exclusion reasons change after the results are read.
failure_modes.cause: Eligibility is being adapted to favor a conclusion.
failure_modes.repair: Restore the original criteria and document any protocol amendment separately.
failure_modes.recheck: The same rule is applied to supportive and contrary studies.

failure_modes.symptom: A numerical synthesis has no common denominator or endpoint.
failure_modes.cause: Unlike measures were pooled without a transformation rationale.
failure_modes.repair: Undo the pooled estimate and give a structured narrative until comparability is established.
failure_modes.recheck: Every numerical comparison retains its population, unit and follow-up.

worked_example.input: Records R1 and R2 share DOI D1. R3 has DOI D2 but reports the same registered cohort K1 at 12 months. R4 is a distinct eligible cohort K2.
worked_example.method: Deduplicate R1/R2, then group D1 and D2 as K1 while retaining both follow-ups.
worked_example.result: There are three unique reports and two independent study families, not four studies. K1 has multiple reports; K2 is an independent contribution.

additional_examples.input: R4 has only an abstract and the protocol requires a verified adult population from full text.
additional_examples.method: Keep its eligibility unresolved until the required population detail can be inspected.
additional_examples.result: R4 is awaiting full text, not an invented exclusion for wrong age. The synthesis uses the confirmed eligible family and explicitly describes the unresolved candidate.

depth.handoff: Preserve the protocol version, original record IDs, dedup and study-family map, exact screening reasons, access flags and extracted locators. Resume unresolved full-text decisions without rescreening settled records.
depth.quality_claim: Original specialist synthesis with source and fixture checks. No matched Muse comparison has been executed; greater domain detail is not measured superiority over upstream packages.
depth.practice_scope: Three authored public exercises cover a standard task, an edge condition and recovery or changed evidence. Their answers are development examples, not held-out results. Supplied-output checks cover only declared facts and invariants; language quality, visual quality and real provider behavior remain separate.

title: Audit a Claim Against Its Actual Evidence
trigger: A factual or completion claim needs an evidence-bounded judgment.
not_for: Treating a popularity signal, search snippet or confident summary as sufficient evidence for a factual conclusion.
inputs: The exact claim and intended audience
The supporting artifact and sources
steps: Split the claim into independently checkable propositions.
Match each proposition to the smallest adequate source location.
Distinguish evidence that a component exists from evidence that it produced the claimed result.
Seek a counterexample or scope mismatch for important propositions.
Return supported wording and the unresolved propositions without rewriting history.
checks: The verdict does not exceed the evidence scope.
A self-authored receipt is not treated as independent authority.
Unsupported does not automatically mean false.
recovery: Report the supported findings and the search boundary. Separate unavailable evidence from evidence of absence, and show what observation would resolve the uncertainty.
example: A report says the whole workflow is complete after unit tests. Check exactly which parts the evidence establishes.
improvement: Adds proposition-level review and narrower corrected language rather than an undifferentiated pass badge.

decisions.when: A paragraph contains several different assertions.
decisions.do: Split it into independently checkable claims: identity, date, measurement, cause and completion. Keep the requested scope.
decisions.avoid: Do not attach one citation to a sentence containing unsupported extra conclusions.

decisions.when: Evidence is direct but stale or superseded.
decisions.do: Record its observation date and the applicable version. Prefer the source that governs the claim's time window, not whichever supports the desired conclusion.
decisions.avoid: Do not erase the older record or present a prediction as a later observed result.

decisions.when: Sources conflict.
decisions.do: Quote only the minimum relevant passages, identify what differs, and test whether population, version or time explains it. Preserve unresolved conflict.
decisions.avoid: Do not average incompatible facts or invent a deciding authority.

decisions.when: A citation exists but does not entail the claim.
decisions.do: Downgrade that claim to insufficient or contradicted and propose the narrow supported wording.
decisions.avoid: Do not promote source presence, a passing unit test or a checksum into proof of all behavior.

decisions.when: The user needs a decision before all evidence is available.
decisions.do: Separate the reversible recommendation from unresolved factual claims and identify the evidence that would change the recommendation.
decisions.avoid: Do not manufacture certainty or block unrelated supported work.

worked_example.input: Build log says 12 local checks passed. The deployment record says deployment was not run. The draft claims “The application is deployed and all checks passed.”
worked_example.method: Split local tests from deployment. Local tests are supported by the actual log; deployment is contradicted by the release record. Give a corrected sentence and retain the unresolved distribution status.
worked_example.result: “The 12 recorded local checks passed; deployment has not been run.” The result cites each record separately and makes no claim about user adoption.

failure_modes.symptom: A long citation appears authoritative but says something else.
failure_modes.cause: Source relevance was not checked against the exact proposition.
failure_modes.repair: Read the cited span and narrow the claim to what it supports.
failure_modes.recheck: Every claim has an entailment judgment, not only a URL.

failure_modes.symptom: A successful fixture is described as production success.
failure_modes.cause: Environment boundaries were omitted.
failure_modes.repair: Restore the actual environment and named test scope.
failure_modes.recheck: Confirm the report does not cross a source/runtime boundary.

failure_modes.symptom: An old failed run is replaced by a new green summary.
failure_modes.cause: Correction was treated as permission to rewrite history.
failure_modes.repair: Keep both and explain the source change that led to the new result.
failure_modes.recheck: The record is auditable without relying on the author's confidence.

depth.handoff: Preserve atomic claim IDs, exact source identity and locators, observation time, disposition, correction and unresolved counterevidence. New evidence changes the current finding without erasing the prior finding.
depth.quality_claim: More explicit procedures and checkable examples; comparative Muse performance has not been measured.
depth.practice_scope: Public regression exercises. Worked answers are for learning; exclude them from comparison sessions.

title: Compare Explanations With Discriminating Evidence
trigger: Several plausible causes or interpretations fit the same observation.
not_for: Treating a popularity signal, search snippet or confident summary as sufficient evidence for a factual conclusion.
inputs: The observed result and timing
Candidate explanations and relevant source records
steps: Write the observation exactly, including timing, units, scope and known measurement limitations.
List plausible explanations supplied by the evidence, including a measurement or selection artifact where relevant.
For each explanation, state at least one prediction that differs from another explanation under specified conditions.
Compare existing observations with those predictions; distinguish contradiction from absence of a measurement.
Select the smallest authorized check likely to separate the leading explanations, including an unaffected control.
Update the matrix from actual results, retaining unexplained findings and a stop condition when evidence cannot discriminate.
outputs: Deliver named hypotheses, their distinct predictions, observed supporting and contradicting evidence, unresolved assumptions and the next discriminating check. State eliminated, still plausible and favored as different judgments; do not convert a favored account into certainty.
checks: Correlation is not silently converted to causation.
A preferred explanation is tested against adverse evidence.
Unknown facts are not filled in to make a story coherent.
The task-specific structured output is checked against source facts or disclosed adjudication, while semantic usefulness still requires human review.
recovery: Carry the observation version, hypothesis definitions, prediction matrix, actual measurements, assumptions and next authorized discriminating check. Never rewrite a prior prediction after seeing its result.
example: Why did usage rise after our redesign? Compare the redesign hypothesis with promotion and measurement changes.
improvement: Add an executable discriminating-test contract and explicit unknown-versus-contradicted accounting rather than ranking explanations by citation volume.

depth.domain_method: Use an explanation-by-prediction matrix. Separate an observation from the hypothesis proposed to explain it, and seek evidence whose expected outcome differs across hypotheses. Record background assumptions, measurement reliability and shared causes. Prefer a low-cost, safe discriminating observation before collecting more nondiscriminating confirmation. Do not assign numerical posterior probabilities without a justified model.
depth.output_contract: Deliver named hypotheses, their distinct predictions, observed supporting and contradicting evidence, unresolved assumptions and the next discriminating check. State eliminated, still plausible and favored as different judgments; do not convert a favored account into certainty.

decisions.when: All hypotheses predict the same proposed measurement.
decisions.do: Choose a different condition, timing or control that yields divergent predictions.
decisions.avoid: Do not call repeated agreement a discriminating test.

decisions.when: A supposedly negative observation was never measured.
decisions.do: Mark it unknown and identify the missing measurement.
decisions.avoid: Do not treat absence of recorded evidence as evidence of absence.

decisions.when: One observation contradicts a hypothesis only under an uncertain assumption.
decisions.do: Expose the assumption and test its relevance before elimination.
decisions.avoid: Do not silently treat a disputed prerequisite as established.

decisions.when: The user needs a decision before uncertainty resolves.
decisions.do: Recommend a reversible action robust across the remaining explanations and state the residual risk.
decisions.avoid: Do not invent certainty to make the answer decisive.

decisions.when: A hypothesis requires intrusive or unsafe testing.
decisions.do: Use passive evidence, supplied records or a safe simulation within the authorized scope.
decisions.avoid: Do not extend the investigation into an unapproved target.

failure_modes.symptom: The report favors whichever explanation was listed first.
failure_modes.cause: Predictions and counterevidence were not compared symmetrically.
failure_modes.repair: Build the same evidence columns for every hypothesis and include a contrary observation.
failure_modes.recheck: Every hypothesis has explicit support, contradiction and unknown entries.

failure_modes.symptom: A repeat measurement adds confidence but separates nothing.
failure_modes.cause: The selected test has identical predicted outcomes.
failure_modes.repair: Replace it with a condition where at least two predictions differ.
failure_modes.recheck: The chosen test has an explicit outcome-to-hypothesis distinction.

failure_modes.symptom: The conclusion jumps from plausible to proven.
failure_modes.cause: Unmeasured assumptions were hidden.
failure_modes.repair: Downgrade the claim and name the next discriminating observation.
failure_modes.recheck: Certainty does not exceed the inspected evidence and assumptions.

worked_example.input: A job runs slowly. H1 predicts slow behavior on both small and large inputs; H2 predicts only large inputs are slow. Both predict the same log message.
worked_example.method: A log-message check cannot distinguish H1/H2; compare a small-input control at the same version and resource settings.
worked_example.result: Choose the small-input timing check. A fast small control contradicts H1 under the stated model but is compatible with H2; the log message alone eliminates neither.

additional_examples.input: No small-input timing was collected, yet a report says H1 is ruled out.
additional_examples.method: Treat the missing observation as unknown and keep both hypotheses live.
additional_examples.result: Neither hypothesis is eliminated. The next action remains the bounded small-input control, not a claimed diagnosis.

depth.handoff: Carry the observation version, hypothesis definitions, prediction matrix, actual measurements, assumptions and next authorized discriminating check. Never rewrite a prior prediction after seeing its result.
depth.quality_claim: Original specialist synthesis with source and fixture checks. No matched Muse comparison has been executed; greater domain detail is not measured superiority over upstream packages.
depth.practice_scope: Three authored public exercises cover a standard task, an edge condition and recovery or changed evidence. Their answers are development examples, not held-out results. Supplied-output checks cover only declared facts and invariants; language quality, visual quality and real provider behavior remain separate.

title: Explain What Changed and Why It Matters
trigger: A user needs a dated comparison of a product, policy or public topic.
not_for: Treating a popularity signal, search snippet or confident summary as sufficient evidence for a factual conclusion.
inputs: The earlier baseline and current sources
The decision or workflow affected
steps: Identify an explicit comparison period and the dated baseline.
Retrieve the current primary source and distinguish announced from effective changes.
Compare substantive differences rather than repeating entire documents.
Explain practical implications and unknown rollout conditions.
Deliver a brief with source dates and no claim of continuing monitoring unless actually scheduled.
checks: Old developments are not described as new.
Announcement and availability are distinguished.
No background watch is implied by a one-time comparison.
recovery: Report the supported findings and the search boundary. Separate unavailable evidence from evidence of absence, and show what observation would resolve the uncertainty.
example: Compare the current product guide with last month’s saved copy and tell me which changes affect my workflow.
improvement: Adds baseline discipline and effective-date handling to a generic latest-news summary.

depth.domain_method:
Compare two explicitly identified states and report meaningful differences without inventing causes. Distinguish added, removed, modified and unchanged items, with stable identifiers where possible. An observation date, publication date and effective date are different fields and should not be silently substituted.

A change summary should explain impact on the user’s actual task, including reversions and uncertainty. Keep observed differences separate from hypotheses about why they happened. When records have been renamed, use evidence of identity rather than guessing that every similar label is the same object.
depth.output_contract: Deliver a concise what-changed table with before/after values, source revisions, affected decisions and unresolved identity or date questions. Include a practical next action only when the observed change warrants it. Preserve unchanged controls rather than implying everything moved.

decisions.when: Both source snapshots are available.
decisions.do: Compare their stable IDs and relevant fields and cite the exact versions.
decisions.avoid: Do not compare a current file with an unlabeled memory of the old state.

decisions.when: A prior item disappears.
decisions.do: Mark removal only within the observed scope and check whether the source listing is complete.
decisions.avoid: Do not equate a truncated result with confirmed deletion.

decisions.when: Only a label changes.
decisions.do: Resolve identity from IDs or documented history before counting it as a new item.
decisions.avoid: Do not inflate change counts through cosmetic renaming.

decisions.when: A value reverts to an earlier value.
decisions.do: Report the reversion as a change from the immediate baseline and preserve the sequence.
decisions.avoid: Do not erase the intervening state from history.

decisions.when: The user asks why the change happened.
decisions.do: Separate supported explanation from plausible hypotheses and name the evidence needed to distinguish them.
decisions.avoid: Do not present causal inference as a retrieved fact.

failure_modes.symptom: The brief says a record was removed when it still exists.
failure_modes.cause: The second snapshot was incomplete or differently scoped.
failure_modes.repair: Reconcile scope and pagination before classifying absence.
failure_modes.recheck: Confirmed removal has complete comparable observations.

failure_modes.symptom: A date in the summary is misleading.
failure_modes.cause: Publication and effective dates were conflated.
failure_modes.repair: Label each date by meaning and preserve unknowns.
failure_modes.recheck: The user can tell when the change applies.

failure_modes.symptom: A summary loses a rollback.
failure_modes.cause: Only the oldest and newest state were compared.
failure_modes.repair: Include the immediate predecessor and the relevant transition.
failure_modes.recheck: The record preserves the actual change sequence.

worked_example.input: A changes from 1 to 3, B disappears, and C appears in complete snapshots v1 and v2.
worked_example.method: Classify by stable IDs and compare values only on shared records.
worked_example.result: A modified; B removed; C added. Reasons for the changes remain unestablished unless separately evidenced.

additional_examples.input: A later snapshot restores A to 1.
additional_examples.method: Use v2 as the immediate baseline, not the original value alone.
additional_examples.result: Report A’s reversion from 3 to 1 at v3; do not label the latest transition unchanged.

depth.handoff: Preserve both snapshot identities, scope completeness, stable IDs, observed differences, date semantics and unresolved explanations. Resume with the next comparable snapshot, not an inferred history.

upstream_items.review_scope: DISCOVERY_INDEX_ONLY; no claim that this is the strongest task-specific competitor

depth.quality_claim: Original task procedures and input-derived public exercise checks. No real Muse comparison, independent semantic superiority, clinical effectiveness or consumer adoption has been established.
depth.practice_scope: Three authored public exercises cover a routine case, a constraint or ambiguity, and a changed-evidence recovery. Their answers are teaching and regression material, not hidden benchmarks. The checker tests supplied structured records only; a person must still assess usefulness, source fidelity and actual visual or interpersonal quality.

title: Synthesize Interviews Without Inventing Consensus
trigger: Interview notes need to become findings while retaining dissent and provenance.
not_for: Treating a popularity signal, search snippet or confident summary as sufficient evidence for a factual conclusion.
inputs: Authorized notes or transcripts
The research question and participant labels
steps: Inventory the supplied transcripts, consent boundaries and participant IDs; mark missing sessions before synthesis.
Read each interview in context and record excerpts with stable locators rather than isolated memorable sentences.
Develop a concise codebook with inclusion and exclusion notes; revise it transparently when a new distinction matters.
Group related codes into themes while keeping each supporting and dissenting participant visible.
Calculate only within-corpus counts using distinct participants and a stated denominator; retain nonresponse and not-asked separately.
Translate the strongest findings into bounded recommendations and unresolved questions, without claiming a tested product improvement.
outputs: Findings with dissent and next questions

Return a theme table with participant IDs and exact excerpt references, observed behavior versus interpretation, divergent evidence, sampling limits and a next research or product decision. Remove identifying details not necessary to the finding. Do not invent demographic personas or effect sizes.
checks: Quotes retain their original meaning.
One vocal participant does not become a majority.
Sample limitations remain visible.
The task-specific structured output is checked against source facts or disclosed adjudication, while semantic usefulness still requires human review.
recovery: Save transcript versions, consent scope, codebook revisions, excerpt locators, participant-level support/dissent and unasked topics. Resume with the missing evidence or decision, not another synthetic persona.
example: Synthesize these six customer interviews into needs, disagreements and the next prototype questions.
improvement: Add explicit participant-denominator and quote-fidelity checks; avoid inheriting unmeasured improvement percentages from illustrative communication examples.

depth.domain_method: Qualitative synthesis preserves the chain from participant and context to excerpt, code, theme and interpretation. Count distinct participants, not repeated quotations, when reporting within-sample prevalence. Separate what someone said from what they did and what the researcher inferred. Negative cases and minority needs can be decision-critical even when uncommon; purposive interview samples do not estimate population prevalence.
depth.output_contract: Return a theme table with participant IDs and exact excerpt references, observed behavior versus interpretation, divergent evidence, sampling limits and a next research or product decision. Remove identifying details not necessary to the finding. Do not invent demographic personas or effect sizes.

decisions.when: One participant repeats the same concern five times.
decisions.do: Count one participant contribution to that theme and keep the repeated excerpts as detail.
decisions.avoid: Do not turn quote frequency into participant prevalence.

decisions.when: Participants disagree.
decisions.do: Describe the conditions and segment context behind both positions; preserve the negative case.
decisions.avoid: Do not manufacture consensus by omitting dissent.

decisions.when: A topic was not asked in every session.
decisions.do: Use an asked-and-answered denominator or state the unbalanced coverage.
decisions.avoid: Do not label unasked participants as having no concern.

decisions.when: A quotation contains identifying or sensitive details.
decisions.do: Use the minimum necessary excerpt and a consent-compatible pseudonymous ID.
decisions.avoid: Do not publish private raw transcripts merely to demonstrate traceability.

decisions.when: A recommendation implies a numeric conversion or satisfaction gain.
decisions.do: Label it a hypothesis and define a subsequent measurement.
decisions.avoid: Do not infer effect size from interview enthusiasm.

failure_modes.symptom: The summary says all users agree but one transcript disagrees.
failure_modes.cause: Theme compression erased a negative case.
failure_modes.repair: Restore the dissenting evidence and narrow the conclusion.
failure_modes.recheck: Participant-level support and dissent remain visible.

failure_modes.symptom: A percentage changes when duplicate excerpts are removed.
failure_modes.cause: The denominator was quotations rather than people.
failure_modes.repair: Recompute unique participant counts and state the sampling limitation.
failure_modes.recheck: Counts can be reproduced from participant IDs.

failure_modes.symptom: The report contains a quote that cannot be found.
failure_modes.cause: Paraphrase was formatted as direct speech or an excerpt was fabricated.
failure_modes.repair: Replace it with a supported paraphrase or exact source quotation.
failure_modes.recheck: Every direct quote matches its inspected source span.

worked_example.input: P1 raises navigation difficulty in two excerpts, P2 raises it once, and P3 reports no difficulty. All three were asked.
worked_example.method: Code the excerpts, deduplicate participant support and keep P3 as a negative case.
worked_example.result: Navigation difficulty is supported by 2 of3 interviewed participants, with 1 dissenting participant. This is a within-sample finding, not a population rate or a proven conversion effect.

additional_examples.input: P3 was not asked about navigation and has no relevant observation.
additional_examples.method: Separate not asked from dissent and recompute the asked-and-answered denominator.
additional_examples.result: Support is 2 of2 asked participants; coverage is 2 of3 overall. P3 is unknown on this theme, not a negative case.

depth.handoff: Save transcript versions, consent scope, codebook revisions, excerpt locators, participant-level support/dissent and unasked topics. Resume with the missing evidence or decision, not another synthetic persona.
depth.quality_claim: Original specialist synthesis with source and fixture checks. No matched Muse comparison has been executed; greater domain detail is not measured superiority over upstream packages.
depth.practice_scope: Three authored public exercises cover a standard task, an edge condition and recovery or changed evidence. Their answers are development examples, not held-out results. Supplied-output checks cover only declared facts and invariants; language quality, visual quality and real provider behavior remain separate.

title: Reproduce a Defect Before Repairing It
trigger: An owned codebase has a reported defect or failing test.
not_for: Unrequested deployments, third-party intrusion, broad rewrites, or executing unreviewed downloaded scripts.
inputs: The relevant source revision and report
Existing test commands and expected behavior
steps: Read the local project instructions and inspect the exact source without overwriting work.
Run the narrowest existing test or observed path that demonstrates the defect.
Reduce the case while keeping the original failure signature and an unaffected control.
Add a regression assertion for the intended behavior.
Record the causal hypothesis, evidence and smallest repair boundary.
checks: The observed failure matches the reported defect.
An unrelated setup failure is not mislabeled reproduction.
The test fails for the intended reason before a fix.
recovery: Preserve the original state and logs. Narrow the failing case, stop after the agreed attempt budget, and return a reproducible next step rather than a speculative broad change.
example: This parser drops the final item. Reproduce the failure on the supplied fixture before changing implementation.
improvement: Adds a negative control and causal failure check to ordinary reproduction-first debugging.

decisions.when: A defect comes with a failing input and expected result.
decisions.do: Freeze the exact input, source revision and caller expectation; run the smallest original entrypoint that exhibits the mismatch.
decisions.avoid: Do not begin by broad refactoring or changing the expected behavior to match the implementation.

decisions.when: The report only says “sometimes wrong.”
decisions.do: Narrow the environment and input dimensions. Use an unaffected control and a bounded repeated run; record not reproduced when no failure appears.
decisions.avoid: Do not turn a plausible theory into a reproduced diagnosis.

decisions.when: The observed failure is an import, setup or permission error.
decisions.do: Report that distinct setup failure and repair the test environment within scope before diagnosing product logic.
decisions.avoid: Do not count any red process exit as reproduction of the reported bug.

decisions.when: A source edit occurs between reproduction and patch.
decisions.do: Re-read the revision and compare the affected code. Rebase the minimal reproducer on the current candidate before editing.
decisions.avoid: Do not apply a stale repair or discard another writer's changes.

decisions.when: The bug is reproduced and code changes are authorized.
decisions.do: Write the failing regression, then the smallest fix and controls. Keep the red output and actual green output tied to source.
decisions.avoid: Do not mark a proposed patch tested or rebuild completed unrelated features.

worked_example.input: A supplied total(items) function returns sum(items[:-1]). The contract says every input item contributes. For [5, 7], expected 12 but observed 5.
worked_example.method: Compare [5, 7] with the empty-list control, then run an assertion on the original function. The missing final slice element is a specific causal hypothesis. Repair to sum(items), then check empty, singleton, mixed sign and multi-item cases.
worked_example.result: The original regression fails with 5 != 12. The minimal patch changes one expression; the five-case fixture suite passes after the patch. This is an owned demonstration, not a claim that a Muse model produced the repair.

failure_modes.symptom: The red test fails before reaching the function.
failure_modes.cause: The environment rather than the behavior is broken.
failure_modes.repair: Repair or report the setup issue, then rerun the original assertion.
failure_modes.recheck: The log identifies the product assertion and actual mismatched values.

failure_modes.symptom: The patch passes but the control changed.
failure_modes.cause: The fix broadened behavior beyond the contract.
failure_modes.repair: Inspect the causal boundary and add a control-specific regression.
failure_modes.recheck: Controls remain unchanged and the reported failure is closed.

failure_modes.symptom: The report contains a green badge without a command.
failure_modes.cause: Evidence was summarized away.
failure_modes.repair: Include source revision, command, exit, assertion, stdout/stderr location and scope.
failure_modes.recheck: A fresh reader can reproduce the original defect without the chat.

depth.handoff: Keep exact input, expected and actual output, source version, environment, regression path, full observed command and exit, controls, patch boundary, and unrun checks. Resume from the current source rather than replaying the old command against changed bytes.
depth.quality_claim: More explicit procedures and checkable examples; comparative Muse performance has not been measured.
depth.practice_scope: Public regression exercises. Worked answers are for learning; exclude them from comparison sessions.

title: Repair the Smallest Causal Boundary
trigger: A reproduced defect has an authorized source boundary and regression test.
not_for: Unrequested deployments, third-party intrusion, broad rewrites, or executing unreviewed downloaded scripts.
inputs: The failing case and source baseline
The change scope and relevant test suite
steps: Read the failing regression, expected behavior and exact source revision; verify that the reproduced defect belongs to the authorized files.
Trace the incorrect value or state to its earliest controllable cause and identify the invariant to restore.
Define unaffected controls and boundary cases before editing; keep unrelated refactoring out of the patch.
Make one maintainable causal change and run the red regression plus controls on the changed revision.
Run the relevant integration and parent checks, inspecting failures rather than treating a green focused test as complete coverage.
Review the diff for accidental behavior changes, preserve remaining failures and deliver exact resume and rollback instructions.
outputs: A bounded repair with regression coverage
A truthful change and test report

Deliver the reproduced failure, causal explanation, exact changed files, focused and relevant broader test results, limitations and rollback instructions. A patch is proposed until executed evidence shows the intended behavior; deployment is a separate effect.
checks: The original failing case now passes.
Nearby valid behavior remains intact.
Skips and unrun integration tests are not reported as passed.
The task-specific structured output is checked against source facts or disclosed adjudication, while semantic usefulness still requires human review.
recovery: Preserve the base and candidate identities, failing command, invariant, patch, unaffected controls, full-suite results and unmerged work. Resume from the first unverified gate, never by resetting the owner's tree.
example: Fix the reproduced off-by-one bug without rewriting the parser, and test empty and single-item inputs.
improvement: Add source-revision and authorized-file accounting to the repair handoff, with a stale-base negative case rather than relying on procedural prose alone.

depth.domain_method: A minimal repair is the smallest change that restores the violated invariant without changing unrelated contracts. Minimal does not mean fewest characters: a short workaround can be less maintainable than a narrow causal fix. Bind the patch to the reproduced source revision and distinguish a regression assertion from the implementation it checks. Preserve controls for behavior that must not change.
depth.output_contract: Deliver the reproduced failure, causal explanation, exact changed files, focused and relevant broader test results, limitations and rollback instructions. A patch is proposed until executed evidence shows the intended behavior; deployment is a separate effect.

decisions.when: The regression passes before any patch.
decisions.do: Recheck input, environment and revision; classify the defect as not currently reproduced.
decisions.avoid: Do not edit speculative code merely to create a visible change.

decisions.when: The source changed after reproduction.
decisions.do: Reproduce against the new revision or rebase the authorized candidate and retest.
decisions.avoid: Do not apply a stale patch to a different baseline without reconciliation.

decisions.when: A fix requires touching an unrelated module.
decisions.do: Explain the dependency and expand scope only when it is necessary and authorized.
decisions.avoid: Do not sneak cleanup or feature work into the repair.

decisions.when: A boundary test fails after the main case passes.
decisions.do: Keep the repair incomplete and inspect the invariant across both cases.
decisions.avoid: Do not weaken the boundary assertion to preserve a green report.

decisions.when: The full suite contains a pre-existing failure.
decisions.do: Compare the same failure at the parent revision and distinguish unchanged debt from regression.
decisions.avoid: Do not erase the failure or claim an all-green suite.

failure_modes.symptom: The patch changes many files without a causal link.
failure_modes.cause: Refactoring was mixed with repair.
failure_modes.repair: Isolate the narrow change and defer independent cleanup.
failure_modes.recheck: Every changed file has a demonstrated role in restoring the invariant.

failure_modes.symptom: Tests pass only after the expected answer is altered.
failure_modes.cause: The test was changed to match the bug.
failure_modes.repair: Restore the accepted contract and derive a legitimate correction.
failure_modes.recheck: The regression still expresses the original intended behavior.

failure_modes.symptom: A stale patch appears to fix a different revision.
failure_modes.cause: Source identity was not checked at application.
failure_modes.repair: Stop application, inspect the current diff and reproduce anew.
failure_modes.recheck: The reported tests and artifact refer to the same exact source.

worked_example.input: At revision r1, an inclusive range parser omits the final value. The regression expects [2, 3, 4] for 2..4; an empty-input control already passes.
worked_example.method: Repair the endpoint calculation in parser.py only, then rerun the inclusive, singleton and empty-input cases.
worked_example.result: The candidate changes parser.py, passes the reproduced case and both controls, and reports broader tests separately. No deployment is implied by the local repair.

additional_examples.input: Before applying the patch, HEAD becomes r2 and parser.py has another owner's edit.
additional_examples.method: Do not overwrite r2; preserve the diff and rerun the reproduction on the new source.
additional_examples.result: Status is source-drift review required, with no applied patch and no stale test result promoted to r2 acceptance.

depth.handoff: Preserve the base and candidate identities, failing command, invariant, patch, unaffected controls, full-suite results and unmerged work. Resume from the first unverified gate, never by resetting the owner's tree.

title: Review a Change for Concrete Failure Paths
trigger: A source diff needs an actionable correctness and maintainability review.
not_for: Unrequested deployments, third-party intrusion, broad rewrites, or executing unreviewed downloaded scripts.
inputs: The exact diff and intended behavior
Relevant contracts, callers and tests
steps: Read changed code together with its callers and invariants.
Trace boundary inputs, failure handling and state transitions.
Separate reproducible defects from preferences or speculative risks.
Propose a minimal reproducer and regression assertion for each material finding.
Return ranked findings with file locations and explicitly note uninspected areas.
checks: Every defect finding has a plausible input-to-failure path.
The review does not claim test execution without output.
Style preferences do not obscure correctness risks.
recovery: Preserve the original state and logs. Narrow the failing case, stop after the agreed attempt budget, and return a reproducible next step rather than a speculative broad change.
example: Review this transaction patch for data-loss paths and show the smallest case for each genuine issue.
improvement: Adds causal traces and evidence grades to generic code-review checklists.

decisions.when: A patch and acceptance contract are available.
decisions.do: Review changed behavior and the paths that call it. Trace one valid input and one boundary input through the code.
decisions.avoid: Do not substitute a generic checklist or review untouched modules without a reason.

decisions.when: A potential defect cannot be reproduced.
decisions.do: Show the prerequisite and source trace, label confidence, and propose the smallest discriminating test.
decisions.avoid: Do not declare a vulnerability or outage from a keyword alone.

decisions.when: The review is meant to be independent.
decisions.do: Use a separate reviewer/context where actually available; otherwise call this a second pass by the same reviewer.
decisions.avoid: Do not obtain independence merely by renaming the role.

decisions.when: A requested change is style-only.
decisions.do: Respect the project's formatter and conventions; keep nits below behavior changes or omit them.
decisions.avoid: Do not block delivery on personal taste.

decisions.when: A fix is applied after review.
decisions.do: Recheck the exact changed region and regression, then close only the corresponding finding.
decisions.avoid: Do not declare unrelated risk categories fixed.

worked_example.input: Function subtotal(items) adds items[:-1] although its contract includes every item. A PR also changes the variable name but not behavior.
worked_example.method: Report the slice on line 2, demonstrate [5,7] gives 5 rather than 12, and explain that every nonempty invoice loses its last entry. Do not demand an unrelated architecture rewrite.
worked_example.result: One blocking correctness finding: total.py:2; evidence input [5,7], observed 5, expected 12; repair sum(items), then test empty, singleton and multiple entries. A clean version must receive no fabricated blocker.

failure_modes.symptom: The reviewer reports many vague issues.
failure_modes.cause: A checklist replaced source tracing.
failure_modes.repair: For each issue, write the specific input, location and consequence; remove unsupported claims.
failure_modes.recheck: The developer can act without asking what failed.

failure_modes.symptom: A correct patch gets a blocker about an absent framework.
failure_modes.cause: Review criteria drifted beyond the brief.
failure_modes.repair: Remove the invented criterion and evaluate the original contract.
failure_modes.recheck: Every blocker maps to a requirement or demonstrable risk.

failure_modes.symptom: All findings disappear after one fix.
failure_modes.cause: Finding identity and source revisions were not tracked.
failure_modes.repair: Reopen the original findings against the new exact revision individually.
failure_modes.recheck: Each closure has evidence specific to that finding.

depth.handoff: Preserve base/head identity, allowed paths, the accepted contract, finding IDs with location and impact, reproduction evidence and the actual reviewer provenance. Revalidate on drift; do not silently review a different change.
depth.quality_claim: More explicit procedures and checkable examples; comparative Muse performance has not been measured.
depth.practice_scope: Public regression exercises. Worked answers are for learning; exclude them from comparison sessions.

title: Design an API Around Consumer Behavior
trigger: A service interface needs an implementable contract or compatibility review.
not_for: Unrequested deployments, third-party intrusion, broad rewrites, or executing unreviewed downloaded scripts.
inputs: The consumer use cases and existing schema
Error, identity and retry constraints
steps: Identify the consumer task, existing version and supplied client assumptions before drafting endpoints.
Specify resource identity and state transitions, including the difference between not found, not allowed and not yet complete.
Define request and response types, required fields, error codes and pagination behavior using the project's existing conventions.
Define retry and idempotency rules: same key/same request, same key/different request, concurrent duplicates and expired retention.
Classify each change against actual consumer behavior; provide migration or tolerant-client tests for uncertain additive changes.
Validate examples against the chosen schema and run available consumer contract tests; separate specification checks from runtime verification.
outputs: Deliver an endpoint or operation contract with examples, required and optional fields, errors, permission boundary, retry policy, versioning impact and consumer tests. Mark proposed semantics as proposed. Do not claim a deployed service, generated SDK or authenticated caller from a schema alone.
checks: Failure responses are distinguishable without parsing prose.
Retry behavior does not duplicate consequential actions.
Compatibility claims include existing callers.
The task-specific structured output is checked against source facts or disclosed adjudication, while semantic usefulness still requires human review.
recovery: Carry the schema version, consumer assumptions, examples, scoped idempotency identity, retention policy, compatibility findings and executed test commands. Resume unresolved consumer or runtime checks without inventing deployment.
example: Design a small task-update API with examples for stale revisions and a lost response after a successful write.
improvement: Add explicit strict-consumer and same-key/different-payload cases; do not claim to replace its entire API-platform scope with one skill.

depth.domain_method: An API contract includes observable request, response, error, authorization, pagination and retry behavior, not only a JSON schema. Evaluate compatibility from the actual consumer's perspective: optional response fields can still break a strict decoder, and enum expansion can break exhaustive clients. Treat idempotency as a scoped relationship among a principal, operation key and canonical request, with explicit retention and conflict semantics.
depth.output_contract: Deliver an endpoint or operation contract with examples, required and optional fields, errors, permission boundary, retry policy, versioning impact and consumer tests. Mark proposed semantics as proposed. Do not claim a deployed service, generated SDK or authenticated caller from a schema alone.

decisions.when: A response adds an optional field.
decisions.do: Check whether known consumers ignore unknown fields; classify compatibility as conditional until tested.
decisions.avoid: Do not assume additive always means nonbreaking.

decisions.when: A retry repeats an idempotency key with different payload.
decisions.do: Return the specified conflict outcome without applying the second effect.
decisions.avoid: Do not silently treat the key as permission to overwrite the first request.

decisions.when: A timed-out write has an unknown outcome.
decisions.do: Reconcile the original operation key through the supported status or readback route.
decisions.avoid: Do not issue a new key and risk duplicate creation.

decisions.when: Pagination crosses changing data.
decisions.do: Specify cursor stability, ordering and duplicate/missing-record semantics.
decisions.avoid: Do not promise a consistent snapshot from an offset-only live list.

decisions.when: No service or client can be executed in this session.
decisions.do: Deliver the complete proposed contract and executable fixture examples where possible, marking runtime checks not run.
decisions.avoid: Do not simulate a remote success and label it integration proof.

failure_modes.symptom: The server and generated client disagree on a required field.
failure_modes.cause: Schema and implementation evolved independently.
failure_modes.repair: Compare the exact versions and restore a shared contract plus a consumer regression.
failure_modes.recheck: Both sides accept and reject the same representative payloads.

failure_modes.symptom: A retry creates two resources.
failure_modes.cause: Operation identity was not retained across retries.
failure_modes.repair: Bind the retry to the original scoped key and document retention behavior.
failure_modes.recheck: Same key/same canonical request returns the original result without another effect.

failure_modes.symptom: An enum addition breaks an existing client.
failure_modes.cause: Exhaustive decoding was ignored in compatibility review.
failure_modes.repair: Add an unknown-value handling path or a versioned migration.
failure_modes.recheck: The old consumer contract is exercised, not just the new schema.

worked_example.input: A create operation has key K1 and canonical payload P1. The first request created resource R1. A retry uses K1/P1; another uses K1/P2.
worked_example.method: Apply the stated idempotency contract within the same principal and operation scope.
worked_example.result: K1/P1 returns the original R1 with no new creation. K1/P2 returns a conflict and also creates nothing. Neither retry receives a new resource ID.

additional_examples.input: An optional field is added to a response consumed by a strict decoder that rejects unknown properties.
additional_examples.method: Treat the consumer behavior as part of the compatibility surface.
additional_examples.result: The addition is breaking for this consumer until the decoder is updated or a compatible representation/version is provided; it is not automatically safe because the field is optional.

depth.handoff: Carry the schema version, consumer assumptions, examples, scoped idempotency identity, retention policy, compatibility findings and executed test commands. Resume unresolved consumer or runtime checks without inventing deployment.

title: Inspect a Real Interface for Access Barriers
trigger: A built interface needs a focused accessibility and usability pass.
not_for: Unrequested deployments, third-party intrusion, broad rewrites, or executing unreviewed downloaded scripts.
inputs: The rendered page or supplied screenshots
Target tasks, viewport and input modes
steps: Identify the specific user journey, required interaction states and requested standard; use the existing implementation rather than inventing a redesign.
Inspect semantic names, roles, states and error associations where source or accessibility-tree access exists; mark screenshot-only limits.
Exercise keyboard traversal, activation, dialog entry/exit and focus return through the actual task, recording what happened.
Check zoom/reflow, contrast, reduced-motion behavior and content alternatives within the requested scope using available tools.
Use a real screen reader or other relevant assistive technology when available; record its actual combination and do not substitute a markup guess for observed speech.
Prioritize barriers by task impact, propose a bounded repair and rerun the affected flow plus an unaffected control before describing it as fixed.
outputs: A barrier report tied to actual states

Deliver a scoped barrier report with reproducible steps, affected task, observed behavior, expected behavior, evidence location, severity and the smallest repair. Include positive controls and an explicit not-tested list. Conformance remains undetermined when required pages, processes or criteria are untested.
checks: A screenshot is not treated as proof of screen-reader behavior.
The main task remains usable at the requested viewport.
Fixes are checked in the rendered interface, not source alone.
The task-specific structured output is checked against source facts or disclosed adjudication, while semantic usefulness still requires human review.
recovery: Preserve the journey, state matrix, tool/browser versions, observed steps, criterion references and unresolved checks. Resume at the missing interaction or repaired flow; do not rerun a whole-site audit or claim universal accessibility from a sampled task.
example: Review this mobile modal for focus, scrolling and toolbar overlap; distinguish measured findings from screenshot-only concerns.
improvement: Add an observation-type contract and negative controls against invented passes; avoid inheriting arbitrary automation-coverage percentages or default-to-failure rhetoric.

depth.domain_method: Accessibility review is evidence about a complete user task across interaction states, not a screenshot score. Separate semantic structure, keyboard operation, focus management, visual perception and assistive-technology observations. Record the actual browser, viewport and assistive technology used. A missing observation is not a pass; an observed barrier is not a claim that every page fails. Use the applicable W3C standard and its exceptions rather than a memorized checklist alone.
depth.output_contract: Deliver a scoped barrier report with reproducible steps, affected task, observed behavior, expected behavior, evidence location, severity and the smallest repair. Include positive controls and an explicit not-tested list. Conformance remains undetermined when required pages, processes or criteria are untested.

decisions.when: Only a screenshot is available.
decisions.do: Review visible contrast, text, hierarchy and layout within its limits; list keyboard and screen-reader behavior as untested.
decisions.avoid: Do not claim keyboard operability or complete WCAG conformance from pixels.

decisions.when: An automated scan reports zero violations.
decisions.do: Continue the manual interaction and assistive-technology checks required by the scope.
decisions.avoid: Do not treat the scan as proof of every criterion.

decisions.when: A dialog closes but focus disappears.
decisions.do: Record the trigger, close action and observed focus target; repair return to the appropriate invoking context.
decisions.avoid: Do not equate disappearance of the dialog with completion of the interaction.

decisions.when: A criterion has an exception or scope condition.
decisions.do: Inspect the current normative wording and document why it applies or does not apply.
decisions.avoid: Do not apply a simplified numeric rule without its conditions.

decisions.when: The user requests an audit only.
decisions.do: Return evidence and proposed repairs without modifying the implementation.
decisions.avoid: Do not redesign, publish or change source under an audit-only request.

failure_modes.symptom: The report marks untested states as passing.
failure_modes.cause: A checklist default was mistaken for an observation.
failure_modes.repair: Change those states to not tested and identify the missing interaction evidence.
failure_modes.recheck: Every pass has a reproducible observed check.

failure_modes.symptom: A fix improves one control but breaks navigation order.
failure_modes.cause: The component was tested in isolation only.
failure_modes.repair: Rerun the full task and focus sequence with adjacent controls.
failure_modes.recheck: The repaired task is operable and the unaffected control remains correct.

failure_modes.symptom: The audit claims a specific screen-reader announcement that was never heard.
failure_modes.cause: Source inspection was promoted to assistive-technology evidence.
failure_modes.repair: Replace the claim with a source-level expectation and mark the runtime check untested.
failure_modes.recheck: Observation type and tool provenance are explicit.

worked_example.input: A modal opens from button A. Keyboard entry, trapped focus and Escape close pass; after close focus lands on the document body instead of A. No screen reader was run.
worked_example.method: Classify the observed focus-return barrier, retain the passing keyboard checks and state the untested assistive-technology dimension.
worked_example.result: The focus-return check fails; screen-reader behavior is not tested; overall conformance is undetermined. The proposed repair restores an appropriate invoking focus target and is verified by reopening and closing the modal.

additional_examples.input: Only a static image of the same modal is supplied, and a report says keyboard and screen-reader checks passed.
additional_examples.method: Separate image inspection from interaction evidence.
additional_examples.result: Those interaction passes are unsupported and must become not tested. Visible observations may still be useful, but no runtime accessibility claim is made.

depth.handoff: Preserve the journey, state matrix, tool/browser versions, observed steps, criterion references and unresolved checks. Resume at the missing interaction or repaired flow; do not rerun a whole-site audit or claim universal accessibility from a sampled task.

title: Check a Release Without Confusing Build and Delivery
trigger: A candidate artifact needs a bounded pre-release review.
not_for: Unrequested deployments, third-party intrusion, broad rewrites, or executing unreviewed downloaded scripts.
inputs: The candidate revision and acceptance criteria
Test outputs, package contents and intended delivery route
steps: Recover the exact candidate, target scope and release checklist already approved for the project.
Verify that every source, test, package and review receipt refers to the same candidate or an explicitly justified unchanged component.
Run required source and runtime checks, including a clean-consumer package exercise where the deliverable is installable or executable.
Inspect migration, rollback and compatibility requirements appropriate to the release; do not impose irrelevant native-host gates on an instruction pack.
Classify every obligation pass, fail, not run or not applicable with its justification and actual evidence.
Issue the scoped readiness decision and, only when authorized, perform the original publication operation and independently read it back.
outputs: Deliver a gate matrix with candidate hash, required checks, observed outcomes, skips and missing evidence, plus a scoped GO/HOLD decision. Report publication separately. A successful check cannot silently waive another required gate.
checks: Test evidence matches the candidate bytes.
Build success is not called deployment success.
Publication is not performed as a side effect of review.
The task-specific structured output is checked against source facts or disclosed adjudication, while semantic usefulness still requires human review.
recovery: Keep the candidate digest, obligation matrix, exact commands and results, qualified package, original publication identifier and rollback conditions. Resume the earliest unresolved gate without rebuilding accepted bytes.
example: Check this release ZIP against the acceptance checklist without uploading or publishing it.
improvement: Add candidate-bound runtime/package obligations and readiness-versus-publication accounting; retain its strong hash and review-scope discipline.

depth.domain_method: Release readiness is a conjunction of independently scoped obligations: exact artifact identity, required source tests, package usability, migration/rollback conditions and intended destination. Source, runtime, deployment and user acceptance are different gates. Bind each result to the candidate it tested. A historical green build does not qualify new bytes, and a ready package is not a published release.
depth.output_contract: Deliver a gate matrix with candidate hash, required checks, observed outcomes, skips and missing evidence, plus a scoped GO/HOLD decision. Report publication separately. A successful check cannot silently waive another required gate.

decisions.when: One required check is skipped on this platform.
decisions.do: Use an applicable qualified platform or keep that gate unresolved; show the supported-platform contract.
decisions.avoid: Do not count a skip as a passing execution.

decisions.when: A package changed after its tests.
decisions.do: Recompute its identity and rerun the checks affected by the changed bytes.
decisions.avoid: Do not attach the old green receipt to the new artifact.

decisions.when: Only source distribution is being released.
decisions.do: Require source, packaging, rights and relevant test gates without demanding an unrelated deployed assistant.
decisions.avoid: Do not recreate the rejected native-installation acceptance criterion.

decisions.when: A release request follows an uncertain publish attempt.
decisions.do: Read the original provider state and artifact identity before retrying.
decisions.avoid: Do not publish twice because the local acknowledgment is absent.

decisions.when: All checks pass but publication was not authorized.
decisions.do: Report ready for the stated scope and leave publication not performed.
decisions.avoid: Do not equate readiness with a public release.

failure_modes.symptom: The report says GO despite a required not-run check.
failure_modes.cause: The gate used majority voting instead of conjunction.
failure_modes.repair: List the missing obligation and hold the scoped release.
failure_modes.recheck: Every required applicable gate has a passing result on the correct candidate.

failure_modes.symptom: A reviewer assessed a different file set.
failure_modes.cause: Review boundaries were implicit or stale.
failure_modes.repair: Provide the exact diff and repeat only the affected review.
failure_modes.recheck: The reviewed paths and candidate hash match the intended release.

failure_modes.symptom: A published asset differs from the tested package.
failure_modes.cause: Distribution bytes were rebuilt or replaced after qualification.
failure_modes.repair: Preserve both artifacts, hold the release claim and reconcile the actual uploaded digest.
failure_modes.recheck: Independent download matches the qualified artifact before release is claimed.

worked_example.input: Candidate H2 needs unit, package and privacy checks. Unit and privacy pass on H2; package passed on H1. No publication occurred.
worked_example.method: Bind the three obligations to their tested artifact identities.
worked_example.result: HOLD: package evidence is stale for H2. Unit and privacy remain valid for H2; publication remains not performed. Rerun the package check against H2 rather than repeating unrelated valid checks.

additional_examples.input: The package check now passes on H2, but an attempted upload timed out.
additional_examples.method: Read the original upload target and compare its digest before any retry.
additional_examples.result: Source readiness can be GO while publication remains unknown until original-provider readback. Do not announce a public release or upload a second copy blindly.

depth.handoff: Keep the candidate digest, obligation matrix, exact commands and results, qualified package, original publication identifier and rollback conditions. Resume the earliest unresolved gate without rebuilding accepted bytes.

title: Turn an Idea Into a Production-Ready Brief
trigger: A creative request needs a clear direction without an unnecessary interview.
not_for: Claiming a plan is rendered media, ignoring reference constraints, or publishing assets without appropriate rights.
inputs: The requested medium, audience and outcome
Supplied references and fixed constraints
steps: Read the request, supplied references and prior decisions; avoid restarting an interview that the material already answers.
List mandatory deliverables and protected elements, including exact wording, aspect ratio, duration or brand assets when supplied.
Translate the intended audience response into concrete hierarchy, composition, typography, imagery or sound choices.
Separate confirmed choices from proposed ones and explain consequential tradeoffs rather than seeking approval for routine reversible details.
Define observable acceptance checks for required content and a bounded creative-review criterion for taste-sensitive choices.
Deliver the complete brief and the next production step, naming any missing asset or decision that truly blocks it.
outputs: A concrete first draft or shot concept

Deliver a self-contained brief naming the audience, intended response, format, exact protected text/assets, confirmed constraints, proposed execution choices, acceptance checks and material open questions. A proposed direction is not user approval, and a brief is not a rendered artifact.
checks: The direction serves the intended audience.
Reference constraints are preserved.
The brief describes visible or audible choices, not only vague qualities.
The task-specific structured output is checked against source facts or disclosed adjudication, while semantic usefulness still requires human review.
recovery: Preserve confirmed decisions with their sources, proposed alternatives, exact protected material, asset rights and the requested deliverable. Resume the specific production step or unresolved conflict rather than another broad branding interview.
example: Turn this product story into a warm 30-second video brief with three concrete opening ideas.
improvement: Add a compact constraint-provenance contract and exact-copy/format conflict cases; do not claim this narrower brief skill replaces the full brand system.

depth.domain_method: A production brief translates intent into observable choices while preserving the authority of each decision. Separate user-confirmed constraints, supplied facts, creative proposals and unknowns. Describe hierarchy, composition, pacing, palette roles and audience response in terms that another creator can act on. Do not use adjectives such as premium or playful as substitutes for visual or narrative decisions.
depth.output_contract: Deliver a self-contained brief naming the audience, intended response, format, exact protected text/assets, confirmed constraints, proposed execution choices, acceptance checks and material open questions. A proposed direction is not user approval, and a brief is not a rendered artifact.

decisions.when: Two supplied constraints conflict.
decisions.do: Expose the specific conflict and offer the smallest viable alternative while preserving both originals in the record.
decisions.avoid: Do not silently discard a mandatory requirement.

decisions.when: The user asks for a finished artifact, not a brief.
decisions.do: Use the brief as an internal production record and continue to the available rendering or implementation tool.
decisions.avoid: Do not present planning as fulfillment of a requested image or video.

decisions.when: A reference shows a style but its rights or identity cannot be reused.
decisions.do: Extract general visual principles and use original assets or authorized references.
decisions.avoid: Do not assume a visible image grants redistribution or identity rights.

decisions.when: The requested tone is broad.
decisions.do: Propose specific visual or narrative choices tied to the audience and mark them as proposals.
decisions.avoid: Do not fabricate audience research or brand history.

decisions.when: The brief is settled and only a format adaptation is requested.
decisions.do: Preserve positioning and protected assets while adapting layout and technical constraints.
decisions.avoid: Do not reopen the entire strategy or replace the approved message.

failure_modes.symptom: A production team cannot act on the brief.
failure_modes.cause: It contains mood adjectives but no concrete choices or deliverables.
failure_modes.repair: Translate each important adjective into visible hierarchy, spacing, imagery or pacing and name the output.
failure_modes.recheck: Another creator can produce a candidate without inventing the core requirements.

failure_modes.symptom: A generated concept changes the supplied tagline.
failure_modes.cause: Protected content was treated as editable copy.
failure_modes.repair: Restore exact wording and add a byte-level text check.
failure_modes.recheck: Every protected string matches the governing brief.

failure_modes.symptom: The handoff marks an unchosen direction approved.
failure_modes.cause: Internal preference was promoted to user authority.
failure_modes.repair: Change the status to proposed and preserve the alternatives.
failure_modes.recheck: Only an actual recorded user decision establishes acceptance.

worked_example.input: The brief requires a1080 × 1920 poster, the exact line "Open Saturday", and no photographs. The proposed direction is geometric shapes with a large date area.
worked_example.method: Keep the size, exact copy and image exclusion confirmed; mark the geometric direction proposed.
worked_example.result: Deliver a vertical vector-style layout brief with "Open Saturday" unchanged, no photo assets, a clear primary message and a legibility check. Approval of the visual direction remains pending.

additional_examples.input: A follow-up asks for a square adaptation but still includes a mandatory vertical-only template constraint.
additional_examples.method: Identify the format conflict rather than pretending both can be satisfied in one canvas.
additional_examples.result: Return a proposed square adaptation separately and ask which governing format applies before claiming conformance; do not change the protected line.

depth.handoff: Preserve confirmed decisions with their sources, proposed alternatives, exact protected material, asset rights and the requested deliverable. Resume the specific production step or unresolved conflict rather than another broad branding interview.
depth.quality_claim: Original specialist synthesis with source and fixture checks. No matched Muse comparison has been executed; greater domain detail is not measured superiority over upstream packages.

title: Translate References Into Reusable Visual Rules
trigger: A user supplies references for an image, interface or visual series.
not_for: Claiming a plan is rendered media, ignoring reference constraints, or publishing assets without appropriate rights.
inputs: The actual reference assets
The target medium and transformation request
steps: Inspect the references and describe observable composition, lighting, palette and material qualities.
Separate the subject identity or fixed details from changeable style choices.
Resolve contradictory references by mapping each to a specific design dimension.
Write a compact visual rule set and asset requirements.
Check a produced sample against those rules without claiming unseen details match.
checks: The reference exists and was actually inspected.
Fixed subject details are not silently replaced.
Style words map to observable properties.
recovery: Preserve the approved version and reference assets. Revise only the failing dimension, state unrendered portions, and offer a usable partial deliverable instead of claiming a finished production.
example: Use these three references to define a consistent look for six scenes while preserving the character’s proportions.
improvement: Adds dimension-specific reference reconciliation instead of a pile of style keywords.

depth.domain_method:
Translate observed visual references into explicit constraints: hierarchy, spacing, shape language, type roles, palette roles, material treatment and composition. Separate measured or visible properties from guesses about fonts, dimensions or hidden components. A reference you cannot actually inspect is an unverified source, not permission to invent its appearance.

Build a coherent design rule set rather than collaging incompatible styles. Identify what must stay invariant and what can vary across screens, frames or assets. Preserve usage and redistribution boundaries separately from the ability to view an image. Visual resemblance alone does not establish rights or accessibility.
depth.output_contract: Deliver a reference-to-rule table, prioritized visual invariants, permitted variation, conflicts between references and an artifact review checklist. When actual files are generated, inspect the render against these rules; a prompt or token list is not visual verification.

decisions.when: The reference is available and clearly observed.
decisions.do: Extract a few high-value rules with the reference location that supports each.
decisions.avoid: Do not invent exact font names or color values from an inaccessible source.

decisions.when: Several references conflict.
decisions.do: Choose which reference governs each role and resolve the conflict explicitly.
decisions.avoid: Do not combine every attractive detail into an incoherent result.

decisions.when: The image is named but not provided.
decisions.do: Use known constraints and mark the missing reference-dependent decisions unverified.
decisions.avoid: Do not claim to reproduce an image you have not seen.

decisions.when: The design must adapt to another format.
decisions.do: Preserve identity and hierarchy while changing layout to fit the new aspect ratio or device.
decisions.avoid: Do not distort the subject or shrink essential content solely to force a fit.

decisions.when: The user wants to redistribute source assets.
decisions.do: Check the specific asset’s rights and consent separately from the design analysis.
decisions.avoid: Do not treat public visibility or an inspiration link as a redistribution license.

failure_modes.symptom: The output looks like several unrelated brands.
failure_modes.cause: Rules were copied without a hierarchy.
failure_modes.repair: Assign a governing source to each visual role and remove incompatible choices.
failure_modes.recheck: The rendered result has a consistent visual logic.

failure_modes.symptom: The assistant claims an exact match without inspecting the render.
failure_modes.cause: Prompt compliance was mistaken for visual evidence.
failure_modes.repair: Open the actual output and compare concrete constraints.
failure_modes.recheck: The verification names observed differences and remaining limits.

failure_modes.symptom: A missing reference is filled with plausible details.
failure_modes.cause: Availability was not checked.
failure_modes.repair: Mark those properties unknown and ask only for the missing asset when essential.
failure_modes.recheck: No invented source property is presented as observed.

worked_example.input: Reference one is visible and supports generous spacing; reference two is unavailable but supposedly supplies a typeface.
worked_example.method: Separate observed rules from missing-source claims.
worked_example.result: Spacing rule supported; typeface choice unverified. Produce a provisional layout without claiming faithful typography.

additional_examples.input: Reference two becomes available but its narrow type conflicts with the readability requirement.
additional_examples.method: Keep the requirement authoritative and adapt the role rather than copying literally.
additional_examples.result: Use the reference’s hierarchy and rhythm with a readable type treatment; document the deliberate deviation.

Identify the indispensable narrative beats and the visual information each shot must communicate.
Create a shot sequence with stable IDs, first-frame occupancy, observable action and continuity state at the cut.
Allocate time in frames or seconds using one stated frame rate; include transitions in the duration calculation.
Check spatial axis, gaze, prop handoff, entry/exit and action feasibility across neighboring shots.
Deliver the complete storyboard, flag any intentionally unresolved production question and specify the smallest test shot before costly generation.

Every shot advances the intended story or information.

decisions.when: A shot contains more actions than its duration plausibly supports.
decisions.do: Simplify to the essential beat or split the shot within the total duration.
decisions.avoid: Do not compress a complex performance into an impossible time block.

decisions.when: A cut reverses screen direction.
decisions.do: Check the geography and crossing rule; add a motivated reorientation or preserve the axis.
decisions.avoid: Do not label an accidental reversal a stylistic choice after the fact.

decisions.when: A recurring prop changes hands.
decisions.do: Specify the handoff or off-screen transition explicitly and carry its state forward.
decisions.avoid: Do not reset prop ownership independently in every shot.

decisions.when: The user already approved assets and geography.
decisions.do: Use those records and proceed to shot direction.
decisions.avoid: Do not reopen the concept interview or invent a new cast.

decisions.when: The request is for a finished clip.
decisions.do: Treat the storyboard as an intermediate artifact and continue through an available authorized production route.
decisions.avoid: Do not claim the storyboard itself is the requested video.

failure_modes.symptom: The timeline exceeds the requested length.
