failure_modes.recheck: Shot durations minus overlaps equal the target within the stated tolerance.

failure_modes.symptom: A character or prop appears without an entry.
failure_modes.cause: Each shot was designed independently of the preceding state.
failure_modes.repair: Add a visible or explicitly motivated transition and recheck adjacent shots.
failure_modes.recheck: Every continuity-sensitive change is accounted for.

failure_modes.cause: Emotion was not translated into observable performance.
failure_modes.repair: Specify gaze, hesitation, breath, posture or action tied to the scene objective.
failure_modes.recheck: The performance can be staged without inferring an invisible mental label.

title: Review Continuity Across a Creative Sequence
trigger: A set of frames, shots or assets needs consistency review.
not_for: Claiming a plan is rendered media, ignoring reference constraints, or publishing assets without appropriate rights.
inputs: The actual sequence and approved references
Known intentional changes across scenes
steps: Create a small continuity inventory of persistent subject and scene attributes.
Compare adjacent shots for appearance, position, direction and state.
Separate deliberate storytelling changes from accidental drift.
Prioritize fixes by viewer-visible impact and dependency.
Recheck corrected frames while preserving already approved material.
outputs: A frame- or shot-specific continuity report
checks: Findings identify the actual frame or transition.
Intentional changes are not marked defects.
Unseen frames are not assumed correct.
recovery: Preserve the approved version and reference assets. Revise only the failing dimension, state unrendered portions, and offer a usable partial deliverable instead of claiming a finished production.
example: Compare these eight frames for character size, clothing and prop continuity before we animate them.
improvement: Adds stateful transition checking and narrow revision scope to general visual QA.

decisions.when: A brief defines persistent character or scene attributes.
decisions.do: Make a continuity card separating invariants from intentional transitions: handedness, prop ownership, costume, screen direction, scale, light and time.
decisions.avoid: Do not treat every visual change as a defect.

decisions.when: The actual frames or audio are available.
decisions.do: Inspect the start, midpoint, end and each cut; compare observations to the continuity card. Record timestamps or frame IDs.
decisions.avoid: Do not accept filenames, shot notes or a render exit as proof of what appears on screen.

decisions.when: Only a shot manifest or someone else's observation notes are supplied.
decisions.do: Perform a scoped manifest/record review and mark direct visual inspection not run. Still flag contradictions present in the records.
decisions.avoid: Do not claim you watched a sequence you could not open.

decisions.when: A violation is localized.
decisions.do: Ask for the smallest affected shot or transition to be repaired, preserving accepted frames and intended motion.
decisions.avoid: Do not restart the entire production or change the approved character.

decisions.when: The sequence passes continuity but export quality is unknown.
decisions.do: Keep continuity, timing, readability, audio and consumer-open checks separate.
decisions.avoid: Do not equate continuity with finished-media acceptance.

worked_example.input: The approved character carries a red satchel in the left hand throughout shots 1–3. Supplied frame observations say frame 001 is left-hand, frame 025 is right-hand, frame 049 is left-hand.
worked_example.method: Locate the discrepancy at frame 025 and ask for a repair to shot 2 only. A later shot intentionally switches lighting from day to night; that approved transition is not a defect.
worked_example.result: Finding: shot-2/frame-025 violates the left-hand invariant. Preserve shots 1 and 3. State that this review used supplied observation records, not newly viewed frames.

failure_modes.symptom: The checklist passes but the rendered prop moves hands.
failure_modes.cause: The review inspected plan metadata instead of frame observations.
failure_modes.repair: Open the actual frames or label direct review unavailable; compare frame-level observations.
failure_modes.recheck: The repaired cut has observed frame IDs, not only a checklist tick.

failure_modes.symptom: Intentional changes are reported as continuity failures.
failure_modes.cause: Invariants and transitions were mixed.
failure_modes.repair: Re-read approved transition notes and narrow findings.
failure_modes.recheck: Each finding violates a stated invariant rather than taste.

failure_modes.symptom: A text storyboard is called a finished animation.
failure_modes.cause: Artifact types were conflated.
failure_modes.repair: Report exactly which files exist and which render/decode checks ran.
failure_modes.recheck: A consumer can open the claimed output format.

depth.handoff: Preserve approved continuity rules, accepted frames, shot and frame IDs, actual observation provenance, unresolved regions, timing and the smallest repair scope. Resume the failed shot; do not regenerate accepted shots.
depth.quality_claim: More explicit procedures and checkable examples; comparative Muse performance has not been measured.

Required format, dimensions, duration and delivery limits
steps: Read the requested output contract and inspect supplied assets before choosing an edit or export path.
Confirm the actual renderer, probe, caption and audio capabilities available; do not infer tools from a skill name.
Build an edit decision list with source in/out points, transitions, audio and caption sources, preserving originals.
Export a new version to a nonconflicting destination with explicit technical settings and bounded resource use.

decisions.when: A requested music or narration track is missing.

decisions.avoid: Do not invent licensed audio or call a silent file complete.

decisions.when: The output aspect ratio differs from the assets.

decisions.avoid: Do not stretch the image or assume the default crop preserves content.

decisions.when: Captions are requested without a transcript.

decisions.avoid: Do not guess dialogue and describe it as accurate captions.

decisions.when: The renderer is unavailable.

decisions.avoid: Do not claim a produced file or substitute a plan without stating the gap.

decisions.when: An upload acknowledgment is missing.

failure_modes.recheck: Complete requires every mandatory technical and content condition.

title: Revise Prose Without Losing Voice or Meaning

The requested voice and protected wording
steps: Read the entire source and determine whether the request authorizes editing or only critique.
Mark exact protected spans, factual claims, uncertainty qualifiers, audience and length constraints.
Choose the smallest structural and sentence-level edits that achieve the requested purpose while retaining the author's register.

Compare original and revised claims, numbers, names and protected spans; repair any semantic strengthening or omitted condition.
Deliver the finished text and a concise material-change note, leaving unsupported claims unresolved rather than embellishing them.

Return the complete requested revision or audit, not advice in place of text. Keep protected spans exact, preserve factual scope and audience, and explain only consequential changes. A style detector is advisory; authorship or truth cannot be inferred from a phrase score.

The requested voice survives.

decisions.do: Return findings and proposed edits without replacing the source.
decisions.avoid: Do not treat an audit request as permission to rewrite or save changes.

decisions.when: A shorter sentence would remove a condition.

decisions.avoid: Do not improve brevity by changing the claim's scope.

decisions.when: A technical command or quotation is awkwardly punctuated.

decisions.avoid: Do not normalize code or quotes under a prose-only request.

decisions.when: The user asks for their voice but supplies no usable sample.
decisions.do: Use already confirmed preferences or state a neutral default and proceed when allowed.
decisions.avoid: Do not infer personal opinions or stylistic traits from unrelated history.

decisions.when: A detector flags wording that is intentionally part of the source voice.
decisions.do: Use editorial judgment and retain it when it serves the brief.
decisions.avoid: Do not optimize a detector score at the expense of meaning or authenticity.

failure_modes.cause: Persuasive wording was mistaken for permission to add facts.
failure_modes.repair: Remove the invented value and restore the supported scope.
failure_modes.recheck: Every number and causal claim traces to the source or separately authorized evidence.

failure_modes.cause: The editor changed punctuation or spacing inside a literal span.
failure_modes.repair: Restore the original span and compare exact bytes.
failure_modes.recheck: Protected material is unchanged unless explicitly authorized.

failure_modes.cause: A generic style template replaced the supplied register.
failure_modes.repair: Restore sentence rhythm and vocabulary supported by the source.
failure_modes.recheck: The revision meets the requested purpose without invented voice traits.

title: Turn Customer Assumptions Into Testable Questions
trigger: A product or service idea needs customer evidence before investment.
not_for: Fabricated customer evidence, deceptive outreach, unapproved spending, or treating proposed commitments as accepted.
inputs: The proposed customer and problem
Existing observations and constraints on outreach
steps: Separate known customer behavior from the builder’s assumptions.
Identify the riskiest assumption that a conversation or observation can test.
Draft neutral questions about recent behavior rather than leading praise-seeking questions.
Define what evidence would change the offer or stop the idea.
Return an interview guide and evidence log; send no outreach unless asked through an authorized tool.
outputs: A decision rule and evidence log
checks: Questions do not assume the proposed solution is desirable.
Hypothetical enthusiasm is not called purchase evidence.
Outreach remains a draft unless actually authorized and sent.
recovery: Separate confirmed evidence from assumptions. Produce a reversible next experiment or draft, and do not turn a missing integration into a reason to abandon useful analysis.
example: Help me test whether small clinics need this document workflow before I build it.
improvement: Adds disconfirmation criteria and behavioral questions to customer-discovery scripts.

depth.domain_method:
Decompose a business idea into assumptions about a specific person, recurring task, current workaround, consequence and willingness to change. Interview evidence should describe actual behavior before soliciting reactions to a proposed solution. Distinguish what participants said, what they demonstrably did, and what they paid for.

Count people and independent observations rather than the number of quotes. A convenient sample can identify useful problems but does not establish population demand. Keep negative evidence, recruitment filters and leading questions visible. A useful outcome is a sharper hypothesis and next discriminating test, not automatic validation of the founder’s idea.
depth.output_contract: Deliver an assumption map, neutral interview questions, source-linked observations grouped by participant, contradictory evidence and a bounded next experiment. Separate direct behavior from opinion and observed willingness to pay from hypothetical enthusiasm. Do not contact participants or store personal details beyond the authorized scope.

decisions.when: The user has only an idea and target audience.
decisions.do: Identify the riskiest behavior assumption and create questions about the last real occurrence of the problem.
decisions.avoid: Do not lead with a sales pitch or ask whether people like the idea.

decisions.when: Interview notes already exist.
decisions.do: Extract observations with participant IDs and preserve exact context before clustering.
decisions.avoid: Do not paraphrase every favorable quote into proof of demand.

decisions.when: Several quotes come from one participant.
decisions.do: Count that person once for participant-level patterns and retain the distinct events separately.
decisions.avoid: Do not inflate support by counting repeated quotations as independent customers.

decisions.when: Participants praise the concept but show no behavior.
decisions.do: Label the evidence as opinion and propose a low-cost test of an actual next step.
decisions.avoid: Do not equate politeness, clicks or hypothetical payment with sales.

decisions.when: Evidence contradicts the initial assumption.
decisions.do: Narrow, revise or stop the hypothesis and retain the disconfirming observations.
decisions.avoid: Do not discard inconvenient interviews to rescue the original story.

failure_modes.symptom: Every interview appears positive.
failure_modes.cause: Questions introduced the desired answer.
failure_modes.repair: Rewrite prompts around recent real behavior and inspect negative or neutral cases.
failure_modes.recheck: The next interview can falsify the assumption.

failure_modes.symptom: A pattern is supported by many quotes but few people.
failure_modes.cause: The unit of analysis drifted.
failure_modes.repair: Deduplicate at the participant level and show the denominator.
failure_modes.recheck: The report distinguishes quote count from independent participants.

failure_modes.symptom: A pilot is declared successful before anyone commits.
failure_modes.cause: Interest was promoted to purchase evidence.
failure_modes.repair: Define a real behavioral success event before the next test.
failure_modes.recheck: The outcome uses the original event and denominator.

worked_example.method: Use participant-level counting and separate opinion from behavior.
worked_example.result: Two participants, one with observed workaround behavior, zero observed paying customers. This is a useful problem signal, not proven market demand.

additional_examples.method: Add the observed payment event without turning one person into a new participant.
additional_examples.result: Two participants, one paying participant. Keep the sample limitation and test whether the problem recurs elsewhere.

title: Shape an Offer Around a Specific Outcome
trigger: A service or product needs a clear, evidence-aware value proposition.
not_for: Fabricated customer evidence, deceptive outreach, unapproved spending, or treating proposed commitments as accepted.
inputs: The intended customer and demonstrated need
Delivery scope, costs and limitations
steps: State the customer’s current problem in their own observed terms.
Define the promised outcome and what is explicitly outside scope.
Connect each included feature to that outcome rather than listing everything available.
Identify proof, onboarding requirements and unresolved pricing assumptions.
Draft a plain-language offer and a small test that could validate its clarity.
checks: Promises match actual delivery capability.
Costs and exclusions are visible.
Unsupported superiority claims are removed.
recovery: Separate confirmed evidence from assumptions. Produce a reversible next experiment or draft, and do not turn a missing integration into a reason to abandon useful analysis.
example: Write a clear offer for a document-cleanup service that cannot promise legal or clinical correctness.

depth.domain_method:
Shape an offer around a specific customer outcome, a deliverable, a service boundary and evidence the provider can actually supply. Separate the promise from a guarantee. Define what the customer contributes, what is excluded, how completion is accepted and what happens when assumptions fail.

Model capacity and contribution economics explicitly. Revenue is not margin: variable delivery cost, fixed setup cost and the number of customers change the scenario. Cash timing and refundable deposits are separate from economic cost. A profitable spreadsheet is only a scenario until demand, execution cost and acceptance are observed.
depth.output_contract: Deliver an offer brief with audience, outcome, deliverables, exclusions, customer prerequisites, acceptance, delivery capacity and transparent price/cost scenarios. Identify unsupported claims and a bounded pilot. Do not invent testimonials, guaranteed results or a payment commitment.

decisions.when: The user has skills but no concrete offer.
decisions.do: Choose a narrow outcome that can be delivered and verified with existing capabilities.
decisions.avoid: Do not inflate the promise to cover every possible customer need.

decisions.when: The scope expands during the discussion.
decisions.do: Separate the core deliverable from optional additions and expose their time and cost.
decisions.avoid: Do not hide extra work behind an unchanged price.

decisions.when: The price exceeds variable cost but fixed costs are material.
decisions.do: Calculate per-customer contribution and the full scenario after fixed cost.
decisions.avoid: Do not report revenue or gross receipts as profit.

decisions.when: Demand would exceed delivery capacity.
decisions.do: Reduce the pilot volume, change sequencing or identify a real resource gap.
decisions.avoid: Do not promise dates that assume nonexistent staff or tools.

decisions.when: The offer depends on an unsupported result claim.
decisions.do: Replace the claim with an honest deliverable or an explicitly tested outcome.
decisions.avoid: Do not manufacture case studies or imply an unmeasured guarantee.

failure_modes.symptom: The offer is attractive but impossible to deliver consistently.
failure_modes.cause: Acceptance and customer prerequisites were vague.
failure_modes.repair: Write an observable done condition and required customer inputs.
failure_modes.recheck: Both parties can distinguish complete delivery from an open-ended promise.

failure_modes.symptom: A high price is mistaken for a healthy margin.
failure_modes.cause: Delivery cost and fixed setup were omitted.
failure_modes.repair: Recalculate contribution and scenario margin with stated assumptions.
failure_modes.recheck: The arithmetic reconciles to price, unit cost and volume.

failure_modes.symptom: A pilot generates more work than the team can handle.
failure_modes.cause: Capacity was not part of the offer.
failure_modes.repair: Cap the pilot and define intake or waiting-list behavior.
failure_modes.recheck: Committed work remains within actual capacity.

worked_example.input: Price is 200 dollars, variable cost is 120, fixed setup is 100, and the pilot has three customers.
worked_example.method: Calculate contribution before comparing the pilot with available capacity.
worked_example.result: Contribution is 80 dollars per customer; scenario margin is 140 dollars after fixed setup. Pilot suitability still depends on supported scope and actual capacity.

additional_examples.input: Five customers request the same pilot but capacity is four.
additional_examples.method: Preserve the economics but evaluate the capacity constraint separately.
additional_examples.result: The scenario may have positive margin, yet the five-customer offer is not delivery-ready. Cap or sequence intake rather than pretending capacity is unlimited.

title: Plan Content From Reusable Source Material
trigger: A creator or organization wants consistent content without inventing claims.
not_for: Fabricated customer evidence, deceptive outreach, unapproved spending, or treating proposed commitments as accepted.
inputs: Approved source material and audience
Channels, tone and sustainable production capacity
steps: Identify the audience questions the source material can genuinely answer.
Select a small set of recurring formats and objectives.
Build each draft from a supported point with a channel-appropriate structure.
Track source reuse and avoid pretending repurposed content is new evidence.
Deliver a manageable calendar and drafts; keep publication separate from preparation.
outputs: A first batch of usable drafts
checks: Claims retain their source meaning across formats.
The production load fits the stated capacity.
No post is represented as published without a real result.
recovery: Separate confirmed evidence from assumptions. Produce a reversible next experiment or draft, and do not turn a missing integration into a reason to abandon useful analysis.
example: Turn this guide into a week of useful posts without exaggerating its results or repeating the same hook.
improvement: Adds source lineage and capacity limits to a generic content schedule.

depth.domain_method:
Build a content system around reusable, verified source material and an audience need rather than a calendar full of invented claims. Treat each content item as a transformation of identified facts, examples or owned creative material. Separate evergreen material, time-sensitive claims and private source context.

Repurposing should preserve meaning while adapting format, depth and channel. A short post must not turn a qualified finding into certainty, and a case study must not silently expose a private client. Draft approval, scheduling and publication are distinct states. Keep source refresh and withdrawal paths so stale claims can be found without redoing unrelated work.
depth.output_contract: Deliver content pillars, a source-to-item map, practical drafts or outlines, channel-specific acceptance checks and a refresh queue. Identify stale, unlicensed or private source dependencies. Record scheduling or publication only when an actual supported service returns evidence.

decisions.when: The user has a substantial source artifact.
decisions.do: Extract reusable claims and examples and assign source IDs before choosing channels.
decisions.avoid: Do not produce a pile of generic posts detached from the source.

decisions.when: A source is outdated or withdrawn.
decisions.do: Hold affected claims and continue content based on still-valid sources.
decisions.avoid: Do not refresh a date without rechecking the underlying fact.

decisions.when: The same idea is adapted to several formats.
decisions.do: Keep the core claim and its qualification stable while changing presentation.
decisions.avoid: Do not count aliases or channel variants as new evidence.

decisions.when: The source contains personal or client details.
decisions.do: Minimize, redact or obtain the appropriate permission for the intended audience.
decisions.avoid: Do not treat access to a document as authority to publish it.

decisions.when: The user requests scheduling or publication.
decisions.do: Prepare the exact content and channel, then use the actual authorized provider and inspect its result.
decisions.avoid: Do not claim a draft exists online or promise a background schedule without execution.

failure_modes.symptom: A polished post contains a claim absent from the source.
failure_modes.cause: The writing process filled a gap with a plausible statement.
failure_modes.repair: Remove or qualify it and trace the remaining claims.
failure_modes.recheck: Every material factual assertion has support.

failure_modes.symptom: Repurposed content contradicts the original.
failure_modes.cause: Compression removed conditions or uncertainty.
failure_modes.repair: Restore the key qualification and check the channel version.
failure_modes.recheck: The shorter format preserves the original meaning.

failure_modes.symptom: Old content keeps circulating after a correction.
failure_modes.cause: Source dependencies were not recorded.
failure_modes.repair: Use the source-to-item map to identify affected drafts and publications.
failure_modes.recheck: The correction scope is explicit and does not erase unrelated content.

worked_example.input: A blog draft uses current source S1; a social post uses stale source S2.
worked_example.method: Check source currency and reuse scope per item.
worked_example.result: The blog is ready to draft. Hold the post for source refresh. Neither item is marked published.

additional_examples.input: S2 is refreshed and approved for reuse.
additional_examples.method: Recheck the affected claim and update the item without rebuilding the blog.
additional_examples.result: Both drafts can proceed; scheduling and publication remain separate authorized actions.

depth.handoff: Preserve source revisions, claim IDs, audience, draft versions, approvals and actual provider publication identifiers. Resume by refreshing only affected claims and reconciling ambiguous prior publishing actions.

title: Design a Service Workflow With Recoverable Handoffs
trigger: A repeated support or operations task needs a clear process.
not_for: Fabricated customer evidence, deceptive outreach, unapproved spending, or treating proposed commitments as accepted.
inputs: Actual examples of the service request
Team boundaries, escalation rules and acceptable outcomes
steps: Map the request from arrival to a verified customer outcome.
Define the minimum information required at each decision point.
Separate routine handling from exceptions requiring a named human or team.
Specify handoff information, response ownership and recovery after interruption.
Test the playbook against a normal case, an incomplete request and a disputed outcome.
checks: Each handoff has an owner and useful context.
Exceptions do not vanish into a generic escalation bucket.
The workflow does not grant new account authority.
recovery: Separate confirmed evidence from assumptions. Produce a reversible next experiment or draft, and do not turn a missing integration into a reason to abandon useful analysis.
example: Create a customer-return playbook using these five real cases, including missing receipts and disputed delivery.
improvement: Adds exception handling and outcome confirmation to a simple process checklist.

depth.domain_method:
Design a service as explicit states, owners, handoffs and acceptance conditions rather than a checklist that assumes every step succeeded. Distinguish ready work from blocked work, proposed ownership from accepted responsibility, and an unknown external outcome from a never-started task.

Use a small state model that fits the actual service. A handoff closes when the recipient acknowledges the required artifact, not when the sender writes a note. Define a recovery path for delays, missing inputs and ambiguous effects. Escalation should identify the specific decision owner and preserve useful independent work.
depth.output_contract: Deliver a service map with step IDs, inputs, outputs, owners, readiness, acceptance and exception paths. Include a compact case record and the next safe action. Do not replace a service’s real task system or invent authority to dispatch people or providers.

decisions.when: A step has verified completion evidence.
decisions.do: Reuse its output and make dependent work eligible.
decisions.avoid: Do not repeat a completed effect because a later local note is missing.

decisions.when: A handoff has no accepted owner.
decisions.do: Mark the responsibility unassigned or awaiting acceptance and identify who must decide.
decisions.avoid: Do not assign responsibility merely because someone was mentioned.

decisions.when: An external operation timed out.
decisions.do: Reconcile the original operation identity and hold only dependent effects.
decisions.avoid: Do not start a replacement with a new identity before knowing the original outcome.

decisions.when: A prerequisite is incomplete.
decisions.do: Keep the dependent step held while continuing independent ready work.
decisions.avoid: Do not flatten the entire service into a single blocked status.

decisions.when: A denial or explicit stop exists.
decisions.do: Preserve it, explain the affected scope and seek the proper decision owner when necessary.
decisions.avoid: Do not route through another account to evade the restriction.

failure_modes.symptom: A task appears complete but the recipient has nothing usable.
failure_modes.cause: Sending and accepted handoff were conflated.
failure_modes.repair: Inspect the actual artifact and acknowledgment.
failure_modes.recheck: The state distinguishes prepared, sent, received and accepted.

failure_modes.symptom: The service duplicates work after interruption.
failure_modes.cause: Original operation IDs and completion evidence were lost.
failure_modes.repair: Recover the last confirmed state before dispatching again.
failure_modes.recheck: No completed or unknown effect is blindly repeated.

failure_modes.symptom: A small exception stalls every customer.
failure_modes.cause: The workflow lacks independent paths.
failure_modes.repair: Separate affected dependencies and continue unaffected cases.
failure_modes.recheck: The hold is limited to the actual prerequisite.

worked_example.input: A draft is complete, sending has an unknown outcome, and an independent chart is planned with an accepted owner.
worked_example.method: Classify the steps from actual state and dependencies.
worked_example.result: Reuse the draft, reconcile the original send, and proceed with the independent chart. Do not resend.

additional_examples.input: The original service later confirms the send completed.
additional_examples.method: Use the confirmation to settle that operation rather than creating another.
additional_examples.result: Draft and send are completed; the chart remains the next ready action.

depth.handoff: Preserve service case IDs, accepted owners, artifact locations, actual state transitions, unresolved original operation IDs and dependency relationships. Resume from the last confirmed state without inventing acknowledgments.

title: Prioritize Work Using Dependencies and Capacity
trigger: A backlog exceeds the available time or resources.
not_for: Fabricated customer evidence, deceptive outreach, unapproved spending, or treating proposed commitments as accepted.
inputs: The backlog and desired outcomes
Dependencies, deadlines and actual capacity
steps: Recover the current backlog, accepted outcomes, dependencies, resource availability and prior completion state.
Validate identities and dependencies, detect cycles or missing prerequisites and separate completed from available work.
Reserve explicitly chosen contingency and nonproject commitments before calculating capacity by resource.
Apply the user's ranking method to feasible items, including prerequisite effort in any selected bundle.
Check the proposed sequence against resource limits and hard dates; expose the displaced work and uncertainty.
Return the bounded commitment and refresh it only when inputs change, preserving the rationale for any reprioritization.
outputs: Deliver an executable selection with dependency order, per-resource capacity accounting, explicit deferred and blocked items, scoring assumptions and one next action. Keep stakeholder preference separate from measured benefit and never turn an estimate into a delivery promise.
checks: The chosen batch fits available capacity.
Scores do not hide unverified assumptions.
Parallel work does not assign two writers to the same artifact.
The task-specific structured output is checked against source facts or disclosed adjudication, while semantic usefulness still requires human review.
recovery: Preserve backlog and score versions, resource budgets, prerequisite closure, completed work and displacement decisions. Resume from the changed constraint rather than rescoring everything to fit a preferred answer.
example: Choose the next three tasks from this backlog while protecting the active release and avoiding duplicate work.
improvement: Add mechanically checkable dependency/resource feasibility and cycle controls; do not adopt fixed success percentages or universal reserve ratios without project evidence.

depth.domain_method: Prioritization first establishes feasibility, then ranks value. Model dependency closure, owner/resource capacity, deadlines and uncertainty before applying scores. RICE, weighted value or cost-of-delay are heuristics whose inputs and units must be stated; they do not create capacity or establish causal impact. A high-scoring blocked task is not executable work, and a dependency cycle needs resolution rather than a reordered list.
depth.output_contract: Deliver an executable selection with dependency order, per-resource capacity accounting, explicit deferred and blocked items, scoring assumptions and one next action. Keep stakeholder preference separate from measured benefit and never turn an estimate into a delivery promise.

decisions.when: The highest-value item depends on unfinished work.
decisions.do: Include its prerequisite closure and total cost, or mark it blocked if the dependency cannot be met.
decisions.avoid: Do not schedule the dependent item as independently executable.

decisions.when: Two tasks need the same scarce person at the same time.
decisions.do: Account for that person's capacity once and sequence or defer the conflict.
decisions.avoid: Do not sum nominal team hours as interchangeable capacity.

decisions.when: A dependency cycle appears.
decisions.do: Report the cycle and identify the decision or split that would break it.
decisions.avoid: Do not manufacture a topological order for a cyclic graph.

decisions.when: Scores are based on uncertain reach or effort.
decisions.do: Show a sensitivity range or alternative ordering rather than false precision.
decisions.avoid: Do not present a decimal score as proof of business value.

decisions.when: A stakeholder adds a mandatory task mid-cycle.
decisions.do: Recompute capacity and state exactly which commitment is displaced.
decisions.avoid: Do not silently add work while preserving the old deadline promise.

failure_modes.symptom: The plan fits total hours but overloads one owner.
failure_modes.cause: Capacity was aggregated across noninterchangeable skills.
failure_modes.repair: Recalculate by resource and move or defer conflicting tasks.
failure_modes.recheck: Every resource stays within its own admitted budget.

failure_modes.symptom: A selected item cannot start despite being ranked first.
failure_modes.cause: Dependencies were ignored during selection.
failure_modes.repair: Add the prerequisite closure or mark the item blocked.
failure_modes.recheck: Every scheduled dependency precedes its consumer.

failure_modes.symptom: A priority score changes without new evidence.
failure_modes.cause: Weights were adjusted to justify a preferred outcome.
failure_modes.repair: Preserve the original scoring rule and document a deliberate policy change separately.
failure_modes.recheck: The ranking can be reproduced from stated inputs and weights.

worked_example.input: A resource has 10 hours. Task A costs 3, B costs 5 and depends on A, C costs 4. The user ranks B above C and requires complete tasks.
worked_example.method: Treat B as an 8-hour dependency bundle A+B, then test whether C fits the 2-hour residual.
worked_example.result: Select A then B for 8 hours and defer C. Do not select B alone or squeeze C into the remaining 2 hours.

additional_examples.input: A depends on B and B depends on A.
additional_examples.method: Detect the cycle before scoring or scheduling.
additional_examples.result: No executable order exists for that pair until a dependency is removed or work is split with authority. Independent task C may proceed if its own prerequisites and capacity permit.

depth.handoff: Preserve backlog and score versions, resource budgets, prerequisite closure, completed work and displacement decisions. Resume from the changed constraint rather than rescoring everything to fit a preferred answer.

title: Review Metrics Without Inventing the Story
trigger: A team needs to understand a performance change and decide what to do.
not_for: Fabricated customer evidence, deceptive outreach, unapproved spending, or treating proposed commitments as accepted.
inputs: The metric definitions and observed data
The decision period and known operational changes
steps: Recover the metric definition, source version, period boundaries and population for each comparison.
Check completeness, missing denominators, event duplication and any measurement-definition change before calculating.
Recompute counts and rates with explicit units, separating absolute, relative and percentage-point changes.
Inspect exposure and relevant segment composition; compare within segments when an aggregate can mislead.
Separate observed association from causal explanation, accounting for concurrent changes and selection effects.
Return a bounded decision and the smallest next measurement that would resolve a material uncertainty.
outputs: Deliver the original figures, reproducible calculations, comparability assessment, supported interpretation, alternative explanations and a decision-relevant next check. Preserve unknown or zero denominators explicitly. Label any recommendation as judgment rather than a measured effect.
checks: Like-for-like periods are compared.
Percent changes include relevant counts.
An action recommendation is distinguished from a proven causal explanation.
The task-specific structured output is checked against source facts or disclosed adjudication, while semantic usefulness still requires human review.
recovery: Keep metric definitions, source versions, period and population filters, numerators/denominators, formulas and open alternative explanations. Resume the missing comparison or calculation, not an unsupported causal narrative.
example: Our support resolution rate fell this month. Check whether case mix or reporting changes explain it.
improvement: Add an analysis-specific arithmetic contract for rates and zero baselines while keeping governed presentation-only work separate.

depth.domain_method: A metric is a numerator, denominator, population, time window and measurement definition. Compare like with like before explaining a change. Distinguish absolute change, relative percentage change and percentage-point change. Decompose aggregate movement by exposure or segment mix where possible; a count can fall while the per-unit rate rises. Causal attribution requires evidence beyond temporal coincidence.
depth.output_contract: Deliver the original figures, reproducible calculations, comparability assessment, supported interpretation, alternative explanations and a decision-relevant next check. Preserve unknown or zero denominators explicitly. Label any recommendation as judgment rather than a measured effect.

decisions.when: The denominator changed between periods.
decisions.do: Report both count and rate changes and explain the different questions they answer.
decisions.avoid: Do not credit a falling count as improved performance without exposure context.

decisions.when: The baseline value is zero.
decisions.do: Report the absolute change and mark relative percentage change undefined.
decisions.avoid: Do not divide by zero, report infinity as a meaningful gain or invent a baseline.

decisions.when: Metric definitions or collection coverage differ.
decisions.do: Mark the comparison noncomparable until a justified common definition is available.
decisions.avoid: Do not combine unlike periods into a precise trend.

decisions.when: A change occurred after a product intervention.
decisions.do: Describe timing and plausible alternatives; require an appropriate design for causal attribution.
decisions.avoid: Do not replace after with because.

decisions.when: A checked analytical source is authoritative and editing is presentation-only.
decisions.do: Preserve its numbers and return calculation disputes to the analysis owner.
decisions.avoid: Do not silently recompute or change governed analysis while polishing a chart.

failure_modes.symptom: The headline improves while the rate worsens.
failure_modes.cause: A count was interpreted without its denominator.
failure_modes.repair: Calculate per-unit exposure and rewrite the headline to preserve both findings.
failure_modes.recheck: The direction of each reported change matches its own calculation.

failure_modes.symptom: A rate difference is mislabeled a percentage.
failure_modes.cause: Percentage points and relative change were confused.
failure_modes.repair: Show the two formulas and correct the label.
failure_modes.recheck: Units and denominators accompany every change.

failure_modes.symptom: The report attributes all movement to one release.
failure_modes.cause: Concurrent changes or selection were ignored.
failure_modes.repair: Narrow the statement to observation and define a discriminating comparison.
failure_modes.recheck: Causal language appears only with appropriate supporting evidence.

worked_example.method: Compute counts and per-account rates separately:0.10 to0.15.
worked_example.result: Ticket count fell 10%; tickets per account rose 50%, an increase of 0.05 per account. This does not establish that a redesign helped or harmed users.

additional_examples.input: The prior period has zero incidents and the current period has three.
additional_examples.method: Use an absolute difference and preserve the zero baseline.
additional_examples.result: Incidents increased by 3; relative percentage change is undefined. Do not report 300% or infinity as a valid comparison.

title: Inspect a Dataset Before Using It
trigger: A supplied dataset is about to support analysis or model development.
not_for: Manufacturing missing observations, silently changing data definitions, or reporting unrun experiments as measured.
inputs: The actual data and data dictionary
Intended use, access restrictions and known collection methods
steps: Identify the intended analysis or model task, available data sources and actual permitted use; record unknown provenance without inventing consent.
Define the unit of observation, stable record key, grouping key, time fields and target label before profiling.
Check schema, types, missing values and duplicate identities; distinguish exact repeats from conflicting records.
Inspect train/dev/test partitions by entity and source family, not just row ID; check whether labels or post-outcome fields leak into features.
Compare coverage and collection times with the target population and decision horizon; document exclusions and unsupported generalization.
Produce the intake decision and a reversible remediation proposal, preserving original bytes and unresolved rights or quality issues.
outputs: A dataset inventory with quality issues
A scoped cleaning and use proposal

Deliver a bounded data card: source and use scope, schema, row and entity counts, duplicate/conflict findings, missingness, partition leakage, temporal limitations and an admit/hold decision for the stated use. Preserve raw input and do not train or upload automatically.
checks: Raw input remains unchanged.
Missing values are not silently treated as zero.
Permitted use and technical suitability are separate questions.
The task-specific structured output is checked against source facts or disclosed adjudication, while semantic usefulness still requires human review.
recovery: Preserve raw digests, data dictionary, grouping and timing rules, allowed-use evidence, conflict list and partition decisions. Resume the specific unresolved check; do not silently resplit a consumed test set.
example: Inspect this survey export before we analyze satisfaction, including duplicate respondents and missing responses.
improvement: Add pre-evaluation entity-group, duplicate-conflict and feature-time checks; do not imply the intake helper performs training or external rights verification.

depth.domain_method: Dataset intake establishes what one row means, how identities and labels were obtained, and whether the data can support the intended use. Separate record IDs from entity or source-family IDs. Duplicate or related entities crossing train/test partitions can invalidate an evaluation even when rows are unique. Provenance, allowed use, temporal ordering, missingness and target leakage are distinct checks; a clean schema alone does not make data fit for modeling.
depth.output_contract: Deliver a bounded data card: source and use scope, schema, row and entity counts, duplicate/conflict findings, missingness, partition leakage, temporal limitations and an admit/hold decision for the stated use. Preserve raw input and do not train or upload automatically.

decisions.when: Different rows represent the same person, source or event family.
decisions.do: Keep the related group in one evaluation partition or explain an appropriate alternative design.
decisions.avoid: Do not treat unique row IDs as proof of independent holdout data.

decisions.when: Two rows share a key but disagree on payload.
decisions.do: Quarantine the conflict and seek the source-owned version or resolution rule.
decisions.avoid: Do not choose the latest file arrival as ground truth.

decisions.when: A feature is only known after the outcome.
decisions.do: Flag target leakage and remove or redesign it for the intended prediction time.
decisions.avoid: Do not retain it because it increases validation accuracy.

decisions.when: The license or allowed use is unclear.
decisions.do: Record the uncertainty and hold the proposed use requiring that permission; continue non-sensitive schema work where authorized.
decisions.avoid: Do not infer rights from public download availability.

decisions.when: The dataset is a small convenience sample.
decisions.do: Bound conclusions to its observed population and identify missing coverage.
decisions.avoid: Do not declare representative performance without evidence.

failure_modes.symptom: Held-out performance is implausibly high.
failure_modes.cause: Entity overlap or post-outcome leakage may be present.
failure_modes.repair: Inspect grouping and feature availability at prediction time before accepting the score.
failure_modes.recheck: No prohibited entity or target information crosses the defined boundary.

failure_modes.symptom: Deduplication silently deletes conflicting records.
failure_modes.cause: Conflict handling was replaced with keep-first behavior.
failure_modes.repair: Restore the originals and separate identical repeats from contradictions.
failure_modes.recheck: Every discarded or held row has a traceable reason.

failure_modes.symptom: The data card says approved but no use scope exists.
failure_modes.cause: Technical cleanliness was confused with permission.
failure_modes.repair: Remove the approval claim and name the unresolved use requirement.
failure_modes.recheck: Technical and rights states are reported separately.

worked_example.result: Hold the evaluation split because E1 crosses partitions. Unique row IDs do not remove leakage; propose a group-aware split without deleting the original records.

additional_examples.method: Check feature availability at the intended prediction time.
additional_examples.result: The split can pass entity isolation while the feature set remains held for target leakage. Do not promote the whole dataset to model-ready from one passing check.

title: Reconcile a Spreadsheet to Its Source Records
trigger: A workbook contains totals, formulas or records that need verification.
not_for: Manufacturing missing observations, silently changing data definitions, or reporting unrun experiments as measured.
inputs: The workbook and source records
Relevant ranges, units and expected reconciliation rules
steps: Inspect the source records, workbook sheets and intended reporting period; identify which fields and formulas are authoritative.
Define a stable matching key and normalize only explicitly equivalent formats, retaining original values and currency.
Detect duplicate identities, missing rows, extra rows and conflicting amounts before calculating totals.
Recompute subtotals with exact arithmetic and inspect formula ranges, hidden rows and excluded records where the workbook interface permits.
Explain differences at row level and distinguish rounding, timing, currency, sign and genuine data errors.
Deliver proposed fixes or apply only authorized narrow changes, then reread affected cells and recheck the reconciliation.
outputs: Deliver a reconciliation table with source row IDs, workbook references, matched/missing/duplicate/conflicting records, totals by currency, formula or range findings and proposed corrections. Preserve originals and require the actual requested authority before changing a live workbook.
checks: Formulas are not replaced by hardcoded results without request.
Units and signs are consistent.
Reconciliation explains residual differences rather than hiding them.
The task-specific structured output is checked against source facts or disclosed adjudication, while semantic usefulness still requires human review.
recovery: Keep source versions, matching keys, original cell references, exact amounts, currency/sign rules and proposed/applied changes. Resume with authoritative readback of the affected rows, not a wholesale workbook rewrite.
example: Find why the monthly total differs from the invoice list without changing the original workbook.
improvement: Add focused row-identity, duplicate and currency reconciliation rather than importing broad investment recommendations or arbitrary finance targets.

depth.domain_method: Reconciliation proves how source records become workbook values. Match stable record identities before totals, preserve currency and sign conventions, and distinguish a duplicate transaction from a legitimate repeated amount. Use exact decimal or integer-minor-unit arithmetic for monetary fixtures. A total can agree while individual rows are wrong, so compare row completeness and formulas as well as aggregates.
depth.output_contract: Deliver a reconciliation table with source row IDs, workbook references, matched/missing/duplicate/conflicting records, totals by currency, formula or range findings and proposed corrections. Preserve originals and require the actual requested authority before changing a live workbook.

decisions.when: Two equal amounts have different transaction IDs.
decisions.do: Treat them as distinct unless source evidence establishes a duplicate.
decisions.avoid: Do not deduplicate by amount alone.

decisions.when: The same transaction ID appears twice.
decisions.do: Compare payloads; mark exact repeats separately from conflicting versions.
decisions.avoid: Do not sum both or silently choose one conflicting value.

decisions.when: Currencies differ.
decisions.do: Reconcile separate currency totals or use an explicitly supplied conversion basis and date.
decisions.avoid: Do not add unlike currencies as though they were the same unit.

decisions.when: A formula omits the final source row.
decisions.do: Show the exact range omission and propose the narrow formula correction.
decisions.avoid: Do not replace the formula with a hard-coded total merely to make it match.

decisions.when: The workbook is read-only or external changes are not authorized.
decisions.do: Return a cell-specific correction proposal and keep actual changes not performed.
decisions.avoid: Do not claim a workbook was repaired from a report alone.

failure_modes.symptom: The grand total matches but a row is missing and another doubled.
failure_modes.cause: Only aggregate checks were performed.
failure_modes.repair: Reconcile record identities and row amounts before trusting the total.
failure_modes.recheck: Completeness and uniqueness pass independently of the grand total.

failure_modes.symptom: A small monetary discrepancy appears inconsistently.
failure_modes.cause: Binary floating-point or mixed rounding rules obscured exact values.
failure_modes.repair: Use integer minor units or Decimal with an explicit rounding policy.
failure_modes.recheck: The same source values produce reproducible totals.

failure_modes.symptom: A repaired workbook still shows the old value.
failure_modes.cause: The edit was not committed or readback used a stale sheet version.
failure_modes.repair: Inspect the original provider revision and affected cell before retrying.
failure_modes.recheck: The authoritative workbook reflects the intended change without duplicate edits.

worked_example.input: Source transactions A=10.10 USD, B=20.20 USD and C=-5.05 USD should appear once each. Workbook rows contain A,B,B,C.
worked_example.method: Match IDs before summing; the source total is 25.25 USD and the workbook total 45.45 USD.
worked_example.result: Report duplicate B and a20.20 USD overstatement. Propose removing the duplicate occurrence only after confirming it is not a separate transaction.

additional_examples.input: A second source contains A=10 USD and B=10 EUR. The workbook reports 20 USD.
additional_examples.method: Keep totals by currency rather than assuming an exchange rate.
additional_examples.result: The reconciled totals are 10 USD and 10 EUR; the 20 USD aggregate is unsupported without a stated conversion basis.

title: Build a Reproducible Analysis Narrative
trigger: A question requires calculations that should be inspectable and reproducible.
not_for: Manufacturing missing observations, silently changing data definitions, or reporting unrun experiments as measured.
inputs: The data and analytic question
Available computation tools and output expectations
steps: Define the measure and comparison before calculating.
Preserve raw inputs and describe each transformation.
Run the calculation using available tools or label unexecuted code as unexecuted.
Check units, sample sizes and a simple independent arithmetic control.
Present the answer, method and limitations with enough detail to reproduce the result.
checks: Results match actually executed computations.
Transformations do not conceal exclusions.
Uncertainty and sample limits survive presentation.
recovery: Retain raw data and the transformation log. Stop the affected calculation on ambiguous units or keys, and continue independent analyses without filling gaps with invented observations.
example: Analyze these task durations and explain the median, spread and outliers with reproducible calculations.
improvement: Adds execution evidence and arithmetic controls to a narrative analysis.

depth.domain_method:
Build an analysis as a reproducible sequence from identified inputs to transformations, checks and conclusions. Preserve the raw dataset, its schema and the unit of observation. Record missing-value handling, exclusions, joins, grouping and the denominator used for every reported metric.

An executable notebook is not automatically a trustworthy analysis. Re-run from a clean state where the tool allows it, detect hidden execution-order dependence, and reconcile totals with independent controls. Separate descriptive results from causal claims and exploratory patterns from a predeclared test. Never silently impute missing data or drop a group to improve a result.
depth.output_contract: Deliver the analysis artifact with data provenance, transformation steps, validation checks, interpretable tables and a conclusion linked to actual results. Provide a clear environment and rerun instruction where code is used. State unavailable inputs or unexecuted cells rather than filling in plausible outputs.

decisions.when: The data is complete and the question is descriptive.

decisions.avoid: Do not expand a simple summary into unsupported prediction.

decisions.when: Observations contain missing values.

decisions.avoid: Do not treat missing values as zero without justification.

decisions.when: A notebook depends on cells run out of order.

decisions.avoid: Do not call a stale visible output a fresh execution.

decisions.when: A join changes the row count unexpectedly.
decisions.do: Inspect key uniqueness and join cardinality before interpreting the result.
decisions.avoid: Do not accept duplicated observations as increased sample size.

decisions.when: The user asks for a causal explanation from observational data.
decisions.do: Distinguish association, assumptions and alternative explanations.
decisions.avoid: Do not infer causation from an attractive chart or a correlation alone.

failure_modes.symptom: The mean changes when blank cells are filled with zero.
failure_modes.cause: The denominator and missingness policy changed silently.
failure_modes.repair: Restore explicit missing-value handling and recompute both quantities.
failure_modes.recheck: Observed count, missing count and metric agree.

failure_modes.cause: Environment, random state or execution order is uncontrolled.

failure_modes.recheck: The difference has an identified cause or remains an explicit limitation.

failure_modes.symptom: A conclusion is unsupported by the displayed table.
failure_modes.cause: Narrative was written before the checked result.
failure_modes.repair: Recompute the claim from the final table and source scope.
failure_modes.recheck: Every quantitative statement reconciles to actual output.

title: Choose a Chart That Preserves the Data’s Meaning
trigger: An analysis needs a clear visualization for a particular audience.
not_for: Manufacturing missing observations, silently changing data definitions, or reporting unrun experiments as measured.
inputs: The checked data and intended message
Audience, display medium and accessibility needs
steps: Choose the comparison the chart should make easy.
Select an encoding appropriate to the variable types and uncertainty.
Check scales, baselines, missing values and category order.
Add units, dates and concise annotations that do not overstate the finding.
Inspect the rendered chart for readability and compare its plotted values with the source.
outputs: A rendered chart or explicit chart specification
A brief interpretation and data note

Labels remain readable in the target medium.
Color is not the only carrier of important meaning.

depth.domain_method:
Select a chart from the question and data structure: changes over ordered time, a relationship between measurements, or comparisons among categories require different encodings. Preserve units, denominators, missing values and uncertainty. A chart’s persuasive appearance must not outrun the underlying observations.

Use position, length and color deliberately. For bar charts, the baseline affects the encoded length; a truncated baseline can exaggerate differences and must be corrected or explicitly handled. A nonzero axis is not automatically wrong for every other chart. Provide an accessible title, explanatory text and, when useful, a data table. Review the actual render for labels, clipping and distinguishability.
depth.output_contract: Deliver a chart or a concrete chart specification with the supporting data, axis units, denominator, source, uncertainty and a brief evidence-bounded takeaway. Include accessible explanatory text. State when only a specification exists rather than claiming a rendered chart was inspected.

decisions.when: The question is change over ordered time.
decisions.do: Use a time-aware view with the actual intervals and mark missing observations.
decisions.avoid: Do not connect absent data as if it were observed without explanation.

decisions.when: The question is category magnitude.
decisions.do: Use a comparison encoding and check the bar baseline and units.
decisions.avoid: Do not exaggerate a small difference with a misleading truncated bar axis.

decisions.when: The question is a relationship between variables.
decisions.do: Use an appropriate scatter view and preserve independent observations.
decisions.avoid: Do not label association as causation.

decisions.when: Important groups have different denominators.
decisions.do: Show rates or denominators explicitly and retain relevant group context.
decisions.avoid: Do not compare raw totals as if exposure were equal.

decisions.when: The chart is generated for a different screen or document size.
decisions.do: Inspect labels, contrast, overlap and the final reading order in that output.
decisions.avoid: Do not certify visual quality from the code alone.

failure_modes.cause: Narrative and encoding were optimized for persuasion.

failure_modes.recheck: The headline survives a direct check against the data.

failure_modes.recheck: The displayed geometry does not misrepresent the quantities.

failure_modes.cause: The final render was not inspected.
failure_modes.repair: Review the actual display size and adjust labels and layout.
failure_modes.recheck: Critical information remains legible without relying only on color.

title: Compare Model Candidates on the Same Frozen Task
trigger: A user wants evidence that a model or prompt change improves results.
not_for: Manufacturing missing observations, silently changing data definitions, or reporting unrun experiments as measured.
inputs: The candidate definitions and evaluation cases
A fixed rubric, resource budget and permissible execution route
steps: Freeze the task set, scoring rubric and candidate identities before evaluation.
Keep development examples separate from the final comparison.
Run candidates under comparable tool access, model settings and budget when supported.
Review actual outputs with blinded labels where possible and retain failures.
Report per-case results, uncertainty and costs; leave unrun outcomes explicitly empty.
outputs: An honest result table or unrun evaluation packet
checks: The candidate did not tune on protected final answers.
All candidates received equivalent inputs and resources.
A configured evaluation is not reported as an executed improvement.
recovery: Retain raw data and the transformation log. Stop the affected calculation on ambiguous units or keys, and continue independent analyses without filling gaps with invented observations.
example: Compare two assistant instructions on the same ten tasks, preserving both failures and token costs.
improvement: Adds paired conditions and unrun-result discipline to casual model rankings.

decisions.when: The decision, cases and rubric already exist.
decisions.do: Use the frozen protocol instead of replanning it. Bind outputs to the exact inputs and candidate revisions.
decisions.avoid: Do not change metrics or delete difficult cases after seeing results.

decisions.when: Candidates differ in model, tools, context or budget.
decisions.do: Name the confound and withhold a head-to-head winner. Finish any descriptive calculations that remain valid.
decisions.avoid: Do not credit a skill for a stronger model or additional tools.

decisions.when: A candidate times out or returns no answer.
decisions.do: Preserve that result in the denominator under the predeclared rule. Distinguish execution failure from incorrect content.
decisions.avoid: Do not silently remove failed cases to improve the average.

decisions.when: Small numerical differences appear.
decisions.do: Apply the predeclared decision threshold and report sample size and per-case outcomes. Use an inconclusive result when the evidence does not separate the options.
decisions.avoid: Do not translate a tiny public fixture gain into a broad capability claim.

decisions.when: The evaluator also authored the candidate and examples.
decisions.do: Label the suite as public regression/development evidence and seek a separate task set/reviewer before a superiority claim.
decisions.avoid: Do not call self-authored answer keys independent ground truth for subjective quality.

worked_example.input: Four closed-label cases have labels A,B,A,B. Plain candidate predicts A,B,B,A (2/4), new candidate predicts A,B,A,A (3/4). The frozen improvement threshold is 0.20 and conditions match.
worked_example.method: Compute 0.50 and 0.75 accuracy with delta 0.25; the candidate crosses this narrow fixture threshold. If one run used another dataset or a different model, report no decision despite the difference.
worked_example.result: The candidate is selected for this four-case protocol only. This does not establish that it is generally better, and these authored inputs are not a protected holdout.

failure_modes.symptom: A missing answer disappears from the report.
failure_modes.cause: Only successful rows were normalized.
failure_modes.repair: Restore every planned case and apply the frozen missing-output rule.
failure_modes.recheck: Case coverage and denominator match the plan.

failure_modes.symptom: The winner changes when a metric is edited.
failure_modes.cause: Post-hoc scoring favored a desired result.
failure_modes.repair: Restore the frozen metric; label the edited analysis exploratory.
failure_modes.recheck: The decision can be regenerated from the original plan and raw results.

failure_modes.symptom: Provider authenticity is claimed from a JSON field.
failure_modes.cause: Metadata declarations were treated as identity evidence.
failure_modes.repair: Describe local consistency only and retain original provider evidence separately.
failure_modes.recheck: The report contains no fabricated authentication or model-run claim.

depth.quality_claim: More explicit procedures and checkable examples; comparative Muse performance has not been measured.
depth.practice_scope: Public regression exercises. Worked answers are for learning; exclude them from comparison sessions.

title: Test Data Transformations Against Explicit Invariants
trigger: A cleaning or migration step may change the meaning or completeness of records.
not_for: Manufacturing missing observations, silently changing data definitions, or reporting unrun experiments as measured.
inputs: The original and transformed data
The intended transformation and invariant rules
steps: Read the actual transformation and source contract, including keys, business version, deletion semantics and permitted scope.
Capture immutable before-state evidence and define invariants appropriate to the operation, not merely a generic row count.
Exercise normal, duplicate, late-arriving, conflicting and empty-window cases using authorized fixtures or supplied records.
Check that newer source versions supersede older ones and identical replays do not create duplicate effects.
Verify that aggregate refreshes replace the exact intended window, including an empty result, while preserving outside partitions.
Report discrepancies and repair the smallest transformation boundary, then rerun the violated invariant and unaffected controls.
outputs: Deliver the transformation contract, before/after invariant results, exact discrepant keys or partitions, accepted replays, quarantined conflicts and a bounded repair. Distinguish a fixture check from production pipeline guarantees such as exactly-once delivery.
checks: Every dropped row has an explicit reason.
Key collisions are not silently resolved.
A successful script exit is not treated as semantic correctness.
The task-specific structured output is checked against source facts or disclosed adjudication, while semantic usefulness still requires human review.
recovery: Preserve input and output digests, key/version semantics, transformation version, authorized window, conflicts and invariant results. Resume the specific failed boundary without silently changing the source contract.
example: Check this cleaned contact table against the original export and account for every removed or merged row.
improvement: Add small portable invariant cases and explicit scope labels; preserve the upstream's stronger pipeline details rather than claiming a universal replacement.

depth.domain_method: A transformation must preserve declared invariants across source identity, business version, payload and aggregation scope. Arrival time is not necessarily business order. Define what may change and what must remain conserved: row membership, keys, units, totals, null meanings and unaffected partitions. Handle conflicting same-key/same-version payloads explicitly; do not invent an order to make a pipeline succeed.
depth.output_contract: Deliver the transformation contract, before/after invariant results, exact discrepant keys or partitions, accepted replays, quarantined conflicts and a bounded repair. Distinguish a fixture check from production pipeline guarantees such as exactly-once delivery.

decisions.when: An older event arrives after a newer one.
decisions.do: Use the source-owned business version and retain the newer state.
decisions.avoid: Do not roll back state based on arrival order.

decisions.when: Same key and version have different payloads.
decisions.do: Hold or quarantine the conflict before any write under the stated policy.
decisions.avoid: Do not choose a winner by filename, timestamp or arbitrary row order.

decisions.when: An identical event is replayed.
decisions.do: Treat it as an idempotent repeat under the exact key/version/payload contract.
decisions.avoid: Do not create another output record or count it as new activity.

decisions.when: A refreshed window contains no eligible rows.
decisions.do: Clear stale aggregate values within that authorized window and preserve outside data.
decisions.avoid: Do not skip the refresh and leave obsolete totals behind.

decisions.when: The requested check concerns a local fixture only.
decisions.do: Report the precise invariants exercised and remaining production assumptions.
decisions.avoid: Do not claim distributed exactly-once behavior from a single-process example.

failure_modes.symptom: A late event restores obsolete data.
failure_modes.cause: Ingestion time was used as business version.
failure_modes.repair: Restore source-version ordering and test a late older event.
failure_modes.recheck: The maximum valid business version remains authoritative.

failure_modes.symptom: A conflict disappears after deduplication.
failure_modes.cause: Keep-last logic erased a contradictory same-version payload.
failure_modes.repair: Preserve both records and apply the declared quarantine policy.
failure_modes.recheck: No conflicting payload is silently admitted.

failure_modes.symptom: An empty sales day retains yesterday's stale aggregate.
failure_modes.cause: The refresh skipped empty outputs.
failure_modes.repair: Replace the complete authorized window, including deletion of stale aggregate rows.
failure_modes.recheck: Inside-window totals reflect current source and outside-window rows are unchanged.

worked_example.input: Key A has version 2 payload20; a late version 1 payload10 arrives, then an identical version 2 payload20 replay.
worked_example.method: Order by source version and compare same-version payload identity.
worked_example.result: Final A remains version 2 with payload 20; the older event is ignored and the identical replay adds no record.

additional_examples.input: Another version 2 event carries payload 25.
additional_examples.method: Detect a same-key/same-version conflict before applying it.
additional_examples.result: Hold the conflicting batch under the fixture's fail-closed policy and preserve the existing state; do not invent version 3 or choose the latest arrival.

Metrics are supported or omitted.
Limitations are explained without burying the demonstrated achievement.

depth.domain_method:
Design a small practice session around a specific skill, an observable target and feedback the person can actually obtain. Separate warm-up, deliberate work and review time. Match difficulty to current evidence rather than assuming that longer or harder practice is always better.

A stop signal such as pain or unsafe equipment takes precedence over the plan; this skill does not diagnose physical symptoms or prescribe rehabilitation.

decisions.when: The person has a clear small target.

decisions.avoid: Do not add unrelated exercises merely to make the plan look comprehensive.

decisions.do: Shorten or defer lower-priority work while retaining useful feedback.
decisions.avoid: Do not silently compress every step below a workable duration.

decisions.when: The task is too easy or too difficult.

decisions.avoid: Do not change several variables and lose the ability to learn from the result.

decisions.when: A physical or equipment stop signal appears.
decisions.do: Stop the affected activity and reassess safety through the appropriate route.
decisions.avoid: Do not encourage pushing through pain or bypassing a safety condition.

decisions.when: The drill improves but unfamiliar performance is unknown.
decisions.do: Use a separate transfer attempt when appropriate.
decisions.avoid: Do not equate repetition gains with general mastery.

failure_modes.symptom: The session feels busy without improving the target.
failure_modes.cause: Too many skills were practiced at once.
failure_modes.repair: Choose a narrower cue and a clear observation.
failure_modes.recheck: The person can tell what changed.

failure_modes.symptom: The schedule cannot fit the available time.
failure_modes.cause: Preparation and review were omitted from the total.
failure_modes.repair: Recalculate the whole session and reduce scope.
failure_modes.recheck: The complete duration stays within the budget.

failure_modes.cause: The standard ignored current level or conditions.
failure_modes.repair: Use a proportionate baseline and compare like conditions.
failure_modes.recheck: Feedback is specific and does not invent failure or mastery.

title: Compare Purchases by Fit and Total Cost
trigger: A user wants to choose between products without unsupported recommendations.
not_for: Making purchases or bookings without approval, guessing current restrictions, or treating uncertain conditions as safe.
inputs: The use case and nonnegotiable constraints
Budget, existing equipment and candidate products
steps: Translate the use case into a small comparison rubric.
Verify current specifications and availability from manufacturer or retailer sources.
Include compatibility, maintenance and recurring costs where relevant.
Compare tradeoffs and disqualify options that violate hard constraints.
Recommend a supported choice or explain the unresolved difference; do not place an order.
checks: Current claims have current sources.
Total cost is not reduced to sticker price when recurring costs matter.
Sponsored claims or reviews are not treated as independent measurement.
recovery: Keep the plan useful with explicit contingencies. Recheck time-sensitive constraints before a commitment and leave purchases, reservations and physical actions to the authorized route.
example: Compare these three devices for my stated workflow, including compatibility and recurring costs.
improvement: Adds fit, disqualifiers and total cost instead of ranking products by popularity.

depth.domain_method:
Compare purchases against the user’s actual use case and hard constraints before optimizing price. Separate must-have features, preferences, compatibility and unknown specifications. Keep exact product variants and evidence dates, because a similar name or old review may describe a different item.

Compute complete comparable costs over a stated horizon: price, shipping, mandatory fees, subscriptions and necessary accessories where relevant. Refundable deposits affect cash required now without necessarily being economic cost. Unknown mandatory charges make a total incomplete, not zero. A low price is not a recommendation if the product does not fit the task.
depth.output_contract: Deliver a small comparison table with fit decisions, supported specifications, complete or incomplete totals, cash requirements and meaningful tradeoffs. State the observation date and source for real prices. Do not place an order, endorse a counterfeit, or promise a return or warranty term that was not verified.

decisions.when: A product fails a stated must-have requirement.
decisions.do: Exclude it from the eligible shortlist and explain the specific mismatch.
decisions.avoid: Do not let a low price override the hard constraint.

decisions.when: A mandatory cost or specification is unknown.
decisions.do: Mark that comparison incomplete and identify the missing fact.
decisions.avoid: Do not substitute zero cost or an assumed feature.

decisions.when: Different options include subscriptions or accessories.
decisions.do: Normalize the horizon and included components before ranking.
decisions.avoid: Do not compare an upfront-only price with a complete multi-period cost.

decisions.when: A refundable deposit is required.
decisions.do: Show it as cash tied up separately from nonrefundable cost.
decisions.avoid: Do not double-count it as permanent expense or hide the liquidity requirement.

decisions.when: The user chooses an option.
decisions.do: Recheck the exact variant, seller, total and terms before any separately authorized order.
decisions.avoid: Do not report a purchase from a recommendation or cart.

failure_modes.symptom: The cheapest option does not solve the user’s problem.
failure_modes.cause: Ranking happened before fit filtering.
failure_modes.repair: Apply hard constraints first and rerank the eligible set.
failure_modes.recheck: Every shortlisted option meets the supported must-haves.

failure_modes.symptom: The checkout total exceeds the comparison.
failure_modes.cause: A mandatory fee or recurring charge was omitted.
failure_modes.repair: Recompute a complete comparable total with dates and horizon.
failure_modes.recheck: Unknown charges remain explicit until verified.

failure_modes.symptom: A review describes a different variant.
failure_modes.cause: Product identity was matched only by a broad name.
failure_modes.repair: Bind evidence to the exact model and configuration.
failure_modes.recheck: The recommendation uses the item actually available.

worked_example.input: A meets the offline requirement and costs 100 plus 20 shipping. B meets it but has an unknown mandatory fee; C lacks offline use.
worked_example.method: Filter by fit and distinguish complete from incomplete totals.
worked_example.result: A has a complete total of 120. B remains unresolved; C is rejected for fit. B is not declared cheapest by assuming its fee is zero.

additional_examples.method: Update B’s complete total without changing the hard requirement.
additional_examples.result: B has a complete total of 100 and is the lower-cost eligible option. No purchase is claimed.

title: Prepare a Clear Appointment Summary
