not_for: Diagnosing conditions, changing treatment, impersonating a professional, or assuming access to another person’s private records.
inputs: The person’s own notes and appointment purpose
Existing professional instructions and questions
steps: Arrange the reported timeline and concerns without diagnosing them.
Separate observations from interpretations and preserve exact supplied instructions.
Identify the questions most important to the person.
Create a concise summary suitable to share with the professional.
Check that no invented medication, symptom or treatment recommendation has entered the summary.
checks: The timeline matches the supplied record.
Professional instructions are not changed.
Urgent concerns are not handled as routine scheduling problems.
recovery: Keep a useful organizational or writing result without presenting it as medical, legal or therapeutic authority. For urgent safety concerns, direct the user to appropriate real-world help.
example: Organize these notes into a one-page appointment summary and questions; do not try to diagnose the problem.
improvement: Adds timeline fidelity and question prioritization while staying organizational rather than clinical.

depth.domain_method:
Organize an appointment around the person’s actual concerns, timeline, current records and questions. Separate observed symptoms or events from interpretation and diagnosis. Preserve dates, duration, relevant context and the source of medication or treatment information without silently resolving conflicting instructions.

A concise preparation summary should help the professional understand priorities, not replace the professional’s judgment. Keep urgent safety concerns ahead of paperwork and direct them to appropriate timely help. Share only the information authorized for the intended recipient. This is a logistics and communication skill, not a diagnostic or prescribing service.
depth.output_contract: Deliver a brief appointment summary, dated observations, medication or record discrepancies, prioritized questions and practical visit logistics. Mark missing dates and uncertain facts. Do not invent a diagnosis, change treatment or claim that a clinician reviewed the note.

decisions.when: The person provides a clear timeline.
decisions.do: Organize it by actual dates and preserve their descriptions.
decisions.avoid: Do not add a plausible onset or symptom that was not reported.

decisions.when: A date or frequency is missing.
decisions.do: Mark it unknown and ask only when it changes the usefulness of the visit summary.
decisions.avoid: Do not turn vague memory into a precise invented history.

decisions.when: Medication records conflict.
decisions.do: Keep both source versions and flag clarification for the appropriate clinician or pharmacist.
decisions.avoid: Do not choose a dose or timing based on which note looks newer.

decisions.when: An urgent safety concern is reported.
decisions.do: Prioritize appropriate timely human or emergency help rather than finishing the document.
decisions.avoid: Do not delay help to complete a checklist or offer an unsupported diagnosis.

decisions.when: The note will be shared.
decisions.do: Check recipient and sharing scope, then report actual delivery separately.
decisions.avoid: Do not claim an appointment occurred or the care team acknowledged the note.

failure_modes.symptom: The summary is long but the main concern is unclear.
failure_modes.cause: All details were treated as equally important.
failure_modes.repair: Lead with the person’s priorities and a short relevant timeline.
failure_modes.recheck: The professional can identify the questions the person wants answered.

failure_modes.symptom: A conflicting instruction disappears in cleanup.
failure_modes.cause: Normalization selected one version without authority.
failure_modes.repair: Restore the discrepancy and its sources.
failure_modes.recheck: No treatment change is disguised as administrative editing.

failure_modes.symptom: The note implies clinical certainty.
failure_modes.cause: Interpretation was promoted to diagnosis.
failure_modes.repair: Return to the reported observation and the unresolved question.
failure_modes.recheck: The summary does not exceed the evidence or role.

worked_example.method: Preserve known timing, mark the missing date and keep the medication discrepancy explicit.
worked_example.result: The appointment note includes both concerns and questions for clarification; it does not choose a treatment instruction.

additional_examples.method: Update the specific uncertainties using their actual source.
additional_examples.result: The administrative gaps are resolved. The note still does not claim a diagnosis or that the appointment has taken place.

title: Prepare a Care Handoff Without Changing the Plan
trigger: People need to coordinate practical support using an existing care plan.
not_for: Diagnosing conditions, changing treatment, impersonating a professional, or assuming access to another person’s private records.
inputs: The authorized plan and practical tasks
The people’s consent, availability and sharing boundaries
steps: Identify the practical coordination request and the existing plan or instructions supplied for it; use only the relevant slice of information.
Record the plan version and source of each clinical instruction without interpreting conflicting orders into a new treatment plan.
Separate practical tasks from clinical questions; route unresolved treatment or medication questions to the appropriate care professional.
Assign proposed practical owners only within the user's stated scope and mark acceptance or acknowledgment accurately.
Prepare the minimum necessary recipient-specific handoff, preserving exact instructions and the care recipient's sharing preferences.
Verify any authorized send or task update at the original destination; keep unacknowledged or uncertain outcomes open and preserve independent work that can proceed.
outputs: Deliver a concise plan-bound handoff with practical tasks, exact existing instructions when needed, owners or pending acceptance, due windows, open clarification questions and sharing status. Do not infer diagnoses, adjust treatment or claim legal/privacy compliance from this workflow.
checks: No clinical instruction is modified.
Sensitive details are shared only within the requested scope.
Proposed responsibilities are not labeled confirmed.
The task-specific structured output is checked against source facts or disclosed adjudication, while semantic usefulness still requires human review.
recovery: Preserve the current plan version, exact instructions, consent/sharing scope, proposed versus accepted owners, original message IDs and open clinical questions. Resume acknowledgments or clarifications without rewriting treatment or replaying an uncertain send.
example: Help organize rides, meals and the written instructions for a family member’s recovery, keeping medical decisions with their clinician.
improvement: Add plan-version fidelity, accepted-owner and delivery-state controls; avoid importing broad medical-response rules or compliance claims without applicable evidence.

depth.domain_method: Care coordination organizes an existing plan without changing clinical instructions. Separate the care recipient, plan version, source authority, practical task, responsible person, consented recipient and acknowledged completion. A family suggestion is not a clinician order, a named owner is not an accepted assignment, and a draft message is not a completed handoff. Preserve minimum necessary information and the recipient's preferences.
depth.output_contract: Deliver a concise plan-bound handoff with practical tasks, exact existing instructions when needed, owners or pending acceptance, due windows, open clarification questions and sharing status. Do not infer diagnoses, adjust treatment or claim legal/privacy compliance from this workflow.

decisions.when: Two supplied care instructions conflict.
decisions.do: Keep both source versions and ask the responsible care professional to clarify before acting on the disputed instruction.
decisions.avoid: Do not average doses, choose by convenience or silently replace an order.

decisions.when: A caregiver suggests a clinical change.
decisions.do: Record it as a question for the care team, not an active instruction.
decisions.avoid: Do not treat a family suggestion as prescribing authority.

decisions.when: An owner is named but has not accepted.
decisions.do: Mark the assignment proposed or pending and identify the needed acknowledgment.
decisions.avoid: Do not call the task covered merely because a name is in the table.

decisions.when: A handoff contains unrelated sensitive details.
decisions.do: Remove information not necessary for that recipient's role and retain the original securely where authorized.
decisions.avoid: Do not distribute the full record to prove completeness.

decisions.when: The user describes an immediate danger or possible emergency.
decisions.do: Prioritize immediate appropriate professional or emergency help over routine planning, using the person's location when necessary.
decisions.avoid: Do not delay urgent assistance to finish a checklist or offer a diagnosis.

failure_modes.symptom: The handoff changes an instruction from the plan.
failure_modes.cause: Summarization introduced a clinical modification.
failure_modes.repair: Restore the exact supplied instruction and route ambiguity for professional clarification.
failure_modes.recheck: No treatment change is introduced by the coordination artifact.

failure_modes.symptom: A task is marked complete but the recipient never acknowledged it.
failure_modes.cause: A drafted or sent message was confused with completed care.
failure_modes.repair: Separate prepared, sent, acknowledged and completed states.
failure_modes.recheck: Each state is supported by the relevant original evidence.

failure_modes.symptom: The same message is sent twice after a timeout.
failure_modes.cause: Unknown external effect was treated as not sent.
failure_modes.repair: Reconcile the original message identifier before any retry.
failure_modes.recheck: No duplicate communication occurs and the original uncertainty remains visible until resolved.

worked_example.method: Keep the instruction unchanged and distinguish accepted transport from pending list preparation.
worked_example.result: The handoff shows Alex accepted, Sam pending, no invented confirmation and no treatment changes. Sharing is limited to the relevant appointment task.

additional_examples.result: No new dose or schedule is issued. The practical transport task can continue, but the disputed clinical instruction is held for the care team.

title: Adapt a Routine to the Person’s Stated Needs
trigger: A person wants an everyday routine made easier to read, follow or carry out.
not_for: Diagnosing conditions, changing treatment, impersonating a professional, or assuming access to another person’s private records.
inputs: The actual task and self-described access needs
Preferred communication format and available supports
steps: Ask about functional needs without inferring a diagnosis.
Break the task into meaningful steps and identify the most difficult transition.
Offer a format suited to the person, such as plain language, larger text or one step at a time.
Remove unnecessary decisions and add a simple recovery option for interruption.
Let the person correct the routine and preserve their autonomy.
checks: Adaptations follow stated needs rather than stereotypes.
The person retains control of decisions.
Simpler presentation does not omit important safety information.
recovery: Keep a useful organizational or writing result without presenting it as medical, legal or therapeutic authority. For urgent safety concerns, direct the user to appropriate real-world help.
example: Make this morning checklist easier to follow with one step at a time and a way to resume after interruptions.
improvement: Adds individualized format and interruption support without assuming disability from limited information.

depth.domain_method:
Adapt a routine to the person’s stated access needs, available supports, preferences and fluctuating capacity. Ask about the task barrier rather than inferring disability or ability from appearance, age or a label. Keep autonomy and the person’s own goals central; an accessible alternative should not unnecessarily remove choice.

Separate essential task outcomes from one conventional way of doing them. Consider modality, environment, pacing, assistive tools and assistance the person actually accepts. Effort units are a user-defined planning aid, not a clinical measurement. Verify real tool or venue features rather than assuming that an accessibility badge guarantees suitability.
depth.output_contract: Deliver a practical routine with compatible steps, adaptation needs, a user-defined effort or time budget, options for variable capacity and an agreed stop or fallback path. Do not infer needs, diagnose conditions or claim a clinical benefit. Preserve existing supports and preferences.

decisions.when: The person has clearly stated access requirements.
decisions.do: Use them directly and identify which steps already fit.
decisions.avoid: Do not request a diagnosis when the functional need is enough.

decisions.when: A conventional step conflicts with the requirement.
decisions.do: Preserve the goal and offer a compatible method or support.
decisions.avoid: Do not abandon the goal merely because the default method is unsuitable.

decisions.when: Capacity varies across days.
decisions.do: Provide a small core version and an optional extension using the person’s own limits.
decisions.avoid: Do not treat a lower-capacity day as noncompliance or failure.

decisions.when: An assistive tool is proposed.
decisions.do: Check that it is actually available, appropriate and acceptable to the person.
decisions.avoid: Do not invent a device capability or assume consent to assistance.

decisions.when: The routine exceeds the agreed effort budget.
decisions.do: Reduce, reorder or defer work while retaining essential outcomes.

A bounded event batch with key, version, value and explicit deletion marker.
steps: Freeze the previous state and incoming batch without mutating either supplied object.
Validate key uniqueness in the state, integer versions and null-valued tombstones.
Detect contradictory same-key/same-version records across the full batch before applying any candidate change.
For nonconflicting input select the highest source version, preserving deletion markers as state.
Calculate duplicate and stale-event counts independent of arrival order and reconcile every applied key.
Hand off the candidate state and conflicts to the existing transaction owner; never mark a database commit from a pure calculation.
outputs: Return a newly calculated state, applied keys, stale-event count, duplicate-event count and any conflicting keys. Conflict returns the original state without partial application. Preserve source and batch digests, version semantics and deletion retention requirements for a real pipeline owner. External writes remain false.
A reproducible JSON report from the named local tool with source assumptions and limits.
checks: Recompute the decisive result from the supplied records and retain counterexamples.
Preserve missing evidence, conflicts and unperformed external actions explicitly.
Separate an executed local calculation from native provider behavior and broad model performance.
recovery: Preserve the exact supplied input and tool version, the returned report, any unresolved source assumptions and the next authorized check. Return a newly calculated state, applied keys, stale-event count, duplicate-event count and any conflicting keys. Conflict returns the original state without partial application. decisions.avoid: Do not partially commit unrelated keys while reporting a single successful batch.

title: Read a Query Plan Before Changing Indexes

Observed cardinalities, representative timings and the workload constraints for reads and writes.
steps: Read the actual query, schema and plan from the same engine version; reject an empty plan.
Classify recognized SQLite access rows without rewriting or dropping the original text.
Distinguish full table access from a covering-index scan, selective search and temporary B-tree sorting.
Locate selective predicates, join order, ordering and covering opportunities in the actual SQL.
Test one justified index change in an authorized disposable database with representative parameter values.
Return observed timings and query correctness separately from the plan classification; retain unknown rows and failed hypotheses.

Include exact SQL/parameter identity, engine version, cardinality, before/after latency and write-cost tradeoffs when those are actually observed. performance_proven and query_executed remain false for text-only inspection.
A reproducible JSON report from the named local tool with source assumptions and limits.
checks: Recompute the decisive result from the supplied records and retain counterexamples.
Preserve missing evidence, conflicts and unperformed external actions explicitly.
Separate an executed local calculation from native provider behavior and broad model performance.
recovery: Preserve the exact supplied input and tool version, the returned report, any unresolved source assumptions and the next authorized check. Return classified supplied plan rows and retained unclassified rows; propose a concrete measurement and index hypothesis only where source evidence supports it. Include exact SQL/parameter identity, engine version, cardinality, before/after latency and write-cost tradeoffs when those are actually observed. performance_proven and query_executed remain false for text-only inspection.

Compare the result with the existing service-owned response policy; distinguish an exhausted budget from an authorized incident action.

title: Size Capacity With Explicit Utilization and Reserve

Target utilization, current instance count, reserve requirement and evidence for load-distribution assumptions.
steps: Verify demand units and that the per-instance measurement represents the same endpoint mix and latency target.
Separate serving instances from reserve capacity and confirm whether reserve may carry normal traffic.
Multiply sustainable throughput by the chosen utilization target before dividing demand.
Round required serving instances upward, then add reserve and compare with current capacity.
Check non-linear bottlenecks, failure-domain requirements and measured saturation behavior before proposing changes.
Deliver the calculation with assumptions, a load-test plan and an explicit no-scale-action status.
outputs: Return required serving instances, total including reserve, additional instances relative to the current count, effective throughput per instance and currently available throughput after reserve. Record workload identity and assumptions in the handoff. No scale action is performed and the estimate is not a price quote.

checks: Recompute the decisive result from the supplied records and retain counterexamples.
Preserve missing evidence, conflicts and unperformed external actions explicitly.
Separate an executed local calculation from native provider behavior and broad model performance.

Return required serving instances, total including reserve, additional instances relative to the current count, effective throughput per instance and currently available throughput after reserve. Record workload identity and assumptions in the handoff. No scale action is performed and the estimate is not a price quote.

depth.domain_method: Translate a workload measurement into a capacity bound, not a purchasing instruction. Add reserve instances only after sizing serving capacity. State linearity and load-balancing assumptions, and distinguish a reserve that remains unavailable for normal load from active redundancy. Latency, queues, storage and shared dependencies need separate measurements.
depth.output_contract: Return required serving instances, total including reserve, additional instances relative to the current count, effective throughput per instance and currently available throughput after reserve. Record workload identity and assumptions in the handoff. No scale action is performed and the estimate is not a price quote.

decisions.when: Demand is exactly divisible by effective capacity.
decisions.do: Keep the exact serving count without adding an unnecessary extra instance.
decisions.avoid: Do not use approximate floating-point division that crosses a ceiling boundary.

decisions.when: A reserve is required during normal operation.
decisions.do: Subtract it from current serving capacity and add it after sizing the required serving pool.
decisions.avoid: Do not double-count reserve as both spare and available throughput.

decisions.when: Demand is zero.
decisions.do: Return zero serving instances plus any explicitly required reserve.
decisions.avoid: Do not invent nonzero traffic or silently remove a declared reserve.

decisions.when: Throughput measurements come from different workload mixes.
decisions.do: Hold the recommendation until comparable measurements or an explicit conservative assumption are recorded.
decisions.avoid: Do not average incompatible benchmarks into apparent certainty.

decisions.when: A shared database or queue saturates before the service instances.
decisions.do: Model and measure that dependency separately and state that horizontal scaling may not help.
decisions.avoid: Do not extrapolate linearly through a known shared bottleneck.

failure_modes.symptom: The scaled fleet still misses the latency target.
failure_modes.cause: The calculation used peak throughput rather than sustainable throughput at the required latency.
failure_modes.repair: Repeat a representative load test and update the measured per-instance input.
failure_modes.recheck: The capacity estimate names the latency objective and actual sustainable measurement.

failure_modes.symptom: An instance failure leaves insufficient headroom.
failure_modes.cause: Reserve capacity was included in normal serving capacity.
failure_modes.repair: Recalculate available throughput after removing the reserved instances.
failure_modes.recheck: The declared failure reserve remains available at the planned demand.

failure_modes.symptom: A tiny input change unexpectedly removes an instance.
failure_modes.cause: Binary floating-point rounding crossed the serving-count boundary.
failure_modes.repair: Use finite decimal inputs and an explicit ceiling operation.
failure_modes.recheck: Boundary cases at and just above effective capacity produce the correct integer count.

Separate likely causes from discriminating observations; propose the smallest reversible diagnostic within the existing authority.

Read actual candidate match counts, visibility, stability and target binding; label fixture observations honestly.
Reject missing, duplicated, hidden, unstable or wrong-target observations before considering preference order.
Choose a deterministic eligible candidate using semantic strategy preference and stable candidate identity.
Have the existing browser adapter refresh the observation immediately before the approved action and verify the resulting state.
Preserve rejected candidates and any page drift so a later turn does not reuse an obsolete locator blindly.

The report never claims a browser action or authenticated target observation. Include actual page/frame identity and observation age in the host handoff where available.

checks: Recompute the decisive result from the supplied records and retain counterexamples.

Return the selected candidate ID or null, all eligible IDs, rejected IDs with reasons and whether more observation is needed. depth.domain_method: Evaluate locator evidence rather than selector string cleverness. A candidate is eligible only when it refers to the intended target, matches exactly one element, is visible and is reported stable. Prefer semantic role, explicit test ID and label strategies before CSS where evidence is otherwise equivalent. Keep rejected candidates with reasons. The supplied observations can become stale; the browser owner must re-observe the target and surrounding context immediately before an authorized action.

The report never claims a browser action or authenticated target observation. Include actual page/frame identity and observation age in the host handoff where available.

decisions.when: A locator matches more than one visible element.
decisions.do: Reject it as nonunique and inspect a narrower semantic scope or frame.
decisions.avoid: Do not choose the first matching element by index without a target justification.

decisions.when: A candidate is unique but points to another control.
decisions.do: Reject the target mismatch even if the selector syntax is valid.
decisions.avoid: Do not confuse a successful selector query with correct user intent.

decisions.when: A control is hidden or still moving.
decisions.do: Request a fresh stable observation before action.
decisions.avoid: Do not click through an overlay or compensate with forced interaction.

decisions.when: Several candidates are eligible for the same target.
decisions.do: Prefer role, test ID or label evidence before CSS and retain the alternatives.
decisions.avoid: Do not claim that a strategy preference proves future stability.

decisions.when: The page navigates or re-renders after inspection.

title: Reconcile an Uncertain Operation Without Replaying It
trigger: A prior connector or application operation has incomplete, contradictory or mismatched result records and must be reconciled before any retry.
not_for: Issuing retry permission, replacing the original TaskGuard or retention system, authenticating unsigned evidence, or treating absence of a result as proof of no effect.
inputs: Original operation ID, exact target and request SHA-256.
Available original-provider observations with matching identities, declared state and receipt identifiers.
steps: Recover the exact original operation ID, target and request digest before issuing any new call.
Read existing provider records and retain their raw source locations and observation times.
Check all three binding fields and quarantine wrong-request or wrong-target evidence.
Separate unknown, started and terminal declarations; detect contradictory terminal outcomes without choosing a convenient winner.
Return the consistency result with retry_authorized false and request original-provider readback.
Continue independent safe work while preserving the unresolved effect and exact resume instructions.
outputs: Return a consistency observation, retained receipt IDs and explicit requirements for provider readback. retry_authorized, provider_evidence_authenticated and external_actions_performed are always false. Preserve original operation identity and unresolved records; never manufacture a replacement ledger, claim or grant.
A reproducible JSON report from the named local tool with source assumptions and limits.
checks: Recompute the decisive result from the supplied records and retain counterexamples.
Preserve missing evidence, conflicts and unperformed external actions explicitly.
Separate an executed local calculation from native provider behavior and broad model performance.

Return a consistency observation, retained receipt IDs and explicit requirements for provider readback. retry_authorized, provider_evidence_authenticated and external_actions_performed are always false. Preserve original operation identity and unresolved records; never manufacture a replacement ledger, claim or grant.

depth.domain_method: Bind every observation to the original operation, request digest and target before considering its state. Deduplicate identical observations, preserve mismatches and classify contradictory terminal reports as conflict. A missing receipt or uncertain observation remains unknown; do not invent a terminal outcome. Even a consistent supplied success record is only a supplied observation, not authenticated provider proof. The original authority must perform provider readback and decide any permitted continuation.
depth.output_contract: Return a consistency observation, retained receipt IDs and explicit requirements for provider readback. retry_authorized, provider_evidence_authenticated and external_actions_performed are always false. Preserve original operation identity and unresolved records; never manufacture a replacement ledger, claim or grant.

decisions.when: No terminal provider record is available.
decisions.do: Keep the observation unknown and require readback under the original operation identity.
decisions.avoid: Do not infer failure or no-effect from a timeout or missing local file.

decisions.when: A receipt refers to another request digest or target.
decisions.do: Classify the evidence set as conflicting and retain the mismatch.
decisions.avoid: Do not reuse a successful receipt from a different operation.

decisions.when: Success and failure are both reported for the same bound operation.
decisions.do: Return conflict and ask the original provider to reconcile its durable state.
decisions.avoid: Do not select the latest arrival as truth without a provider-owned ordering contract.

decisions.when: An identical observation appears multiple times.
decisions.do: Deduplicate the observation without treating repetition as independent confirmation.
decisions.avoid: Do not count copied receipts as extra evidence of execution.

decisions.when: A supplied record consistently reports success with a receipt ID.
decisions.do: Report the supplied success observation while preserving unauthenticated-evidence and no-retry boundaries.
decisions.avoid: Do not upgrade a locally provided JSON record into an authenticated completion or grant.

failure_modes.symptom: An operation is executed twice after a network timeout.
failure_modes.cause: The caller retried before recovering the original provider outcome.
failure_modes.repair: Stop new retries and inspect the original operation and target readback.
failure_modes.recheck: The unresolved effect remains fenced and no second operation is created by this tool.

failure_modes.symptom: A completion report points to unrelated output.
failure_modes.cause: Receipt identity was matched only by a display name or partial key.
failure_modes.repair: Rebind operation ID, full request digest and target to the exact original record.
failure_modes.recheck: Mismatched evidence produces conflict rather than successful completion.

failure_modes.symptom: Deleted history is interpreted as permission to start over.
failure_modes.cause: Retention erased the evidence needed to distinguish a replay from new work.
failure_modes.repair: Preserve the hold and consult original retention/tombstone policy instead of fabricating history.
failure_modes.recheck: No local absence can make retry_authorized true.

worked_example.input: An operation has a request digest but only an unknown observation with no receipt.
worked_example.method: Match the original identity and retain the missing terminal outcome.
worked_example.result: The result remains unknown, requires provider readback and never authorizes retry.

additional_examples.input: Two bound records declare success and failure under the same request digest.
additional_examples.method: Preserve the contradiction rather than choosing a winner.
additional_examples.result: The result is conflict with both evidence identities retained and no external action performed.

title: Check Real Color Tokens Before Interface Handoff
trigger: An interface palette needs reproducible contrast checks against explicit foreground/background token pairs before implementation or review.
not_for: Certifying full accessibility, judging an unseen screenshot, or treating opaque token arithmetic as proof for gradients, opacity or unobserved rendering.
inputs: Named opaque six-digit sRGB color tokens and the actual pairs used together.
The required minimum ratio for each use, plus typography, component state and rendered evidence where available.
steps: Inventory the actual token values and foreground/background combinations rather than checking every color arbitrarily.
Confirm opaque six-digit sRGB inputs and an explicit threshold appropriate to the declared use.
Linearize channels, calculate relative luminance and compute the lighter/darker contrast ratio.
Compare the full-precision ratio with the threshold; show rounded values only as presentation.
Inspect actual rendered normal, hover, focus, disabled and error states through a supported browser when available.
Deliver token findings and proposed fixes separately from full accessibility conformance and actual rendered-state evidence.
outputs: Return every checked pair with token identities, calculated ratio, threshold and pass/fail result. Include an overall calculation result while keeping conformance_certified and rendered_ui_inspected false. The design handoff should also identify real component states and any missing browser, keyboard or visual inspection.
A reproducible JSON report from the named local tool with source assumptions and limits.
checks: Recompute the decisive result from the supplied records and retain counterexamples.
Preserve missing evidence, conflicts and unperformed external actions explicitly.
Separate an executed local calculation from native provider behavior and broad model performance.
recovery: Preserve the exact supplied input and tool version, the returned report, any unresolved source assumptions and the next authorized check. Return every checked pair with token identities, calculated ratio, threshold and pass/fail result. Include an overall calculation result while keeping conformance_certified and rendered_ui_inspected false. The design handoff should also identify real component states and any missing browser, keyboard or visual inspection.
example: Black text token #000000 on white #ffffff has a supplied threshold of 4.5.
improvement: An original task-specific procedure paired with a bounded executable tool, discriminating public exercises and explicit outcome limits.

depth.domain_method: Calculate contrast from the actual foreground and background values, using sRGB linearization and relative luminance rather than visual intuition. Keep pair identity and caller-selected thresholds explicit. Compare the unrounded ratio to the threshold and round only the displayed value. Reject unsupported alpha, gradient and non-sRGB inputs instead of approximating them silently. A token pass says nothing by itself about font size, focus, semantics, keyboard behavior or the real composited screen.
depth.output_contract: Return every checked pair with token identities, calculated ratio, threshold and pass/fail result. Include an overall calculation result while keeping conformance_certified and rendered_ui_inspected false. The design handoff should also identify real component states and any missing browser, keyboard or visual inspection.

decisions.when: A pair passes numerically but the rendered UI uses opacity.
decisions.do: Reconstruct or measure the actual composited colors before claiming that rendered pair passes.
decisions.avoid: Do not apply opaque-token arithmetic to translucent layers without qualification.

decisions.when: The displayed rounded ratio equals the minimum.
decisions.do: Use the unrounded computed ratio for the decision.
decisions.avoid: Do not round a slightly failing value upward into a pass.

decisions.when: A token uses a gradient, alpha channel or unsupported color space.
decisions.do: Refuse the bounded calculation and request the actual supported colors or an appropriate renderer measurement.
decisions.avoid: Do not silently discard alpha or convert color spaces by guessing.

decisions.when: All supplied pairs pass.
decisions.do: Report those calculated pairs as passing and keep other accessibility dimensions open.
decisions.avoid: Do not certify keyboard navigation, semantics or focus behavior from a color check.

decisions.when: A correction would damage the product hierarchy or brand intent.
decisions.do: Offer measured alternatives that preserve semantic role and compare them in the real component.
decisions.avoid: Do not solve one ratio by making every interface color identical.

failure_modes.symptom: Text remains hard to read despite a passing palette sheet.
failure_modes.cause: The inspected tokens were not the colors actually adjacent in the rendered state.
failure_modes.repair: Trace the component styles and inspect real compositing and background variants.
failure_modes.recheck: The measured pair matches the actual component and state.

failure_modes.symptom: A borderline pair is incorrectly reported as passing.
failure_modes.cause: The checker rounded the ratio before threshold comparison.
failure_modes.repair: Compare the full-precision value and retain the exact threshold.
failure_modes.recheck: A value below the threshold remains a failure even when its displayed ratio rounds upward.

failure_modes.symptom: A palette check is presented as complete accessibility approval.
failure_modes.cause: A narrow numeric result was promoted to a broad conformance claim.
failure_modes.repair: Separate token results from keyboard, semantics, zoom, focus and screen-reader evidence.
failure_modes.recheck: The report retains explicit untested dimensions and conformance_certified false.

worked_example.input: Black text token #000000 on white #ffffff has a supplied threshold of 4.5.
worked_example.method: Compute luminance for both opaque sRGB tokens and compare the unrounded ratio.
worked_example.result: The ratio is 21 and the pair passes; the tool does not claim the rendered interface or full accessibility was inspected.

additional_examples.input: Muted text #aaaaaa is paired with white at the same threshold.
additional_examples.method: Calculate the actual token pair instead of judging its appearance from a palette label.
additional_examples.result: The pair fails the requested ratio, and a designer must choose and inspect a suitable replacement in context.

title: Review Interface States and Recovery Paths
trigger: An interface flow needs an explicit state graph covering entry, loading, success, empty, error and recovery behavior before implementation or QA.
not_for: Claiming a browser flow was exercised, inferring screen-reader behavior from a diagram, or treating a complete declared graph as proof of a working application.
inputs: Declared states, initial state, terminal states and the required-state checklist.
Event-labeled transitions, actual component behavior and any observed failure or recovery evidence.
steps: Define the user goal and enumerate actual states, including absence, loading, failure and cancellation where relevant.
Choose one initial state, mark terminal states explicitly and freeze the required-state checklist.
Describe each transition as origin, event and target; reject missing identities and nondeterministic duplicate events.
Traverse reachable states and identify missing requirements, unreachable screens and nonterminal dead ends.
Add meaningful recovery transitions and verify that the design preserves entered data and user orientation where required.
Exercise the implemented flow in a real browser or device separately; return specification findings without inventing runtime coverage.

A complete design handoff includes each state purpose, visible feedback, event contract, error recovery, focus behavior and the exact runtime checks still needed.

Preserve missing evidence, conflicts and unperformed external actions explicitly.
Separate an executed local calculation from native provider behavior and broad model performance.
recovery: Preserve the exact supplied input and tool version, the returned report, any unresolved source assumptions and the next authorized check. Return reachable and unreachable states, missing required states, nonterminal dead ends and a scoped declared-graph status. browser_tested is always false. A complete design handoff includes each state purpose, visible feedback, event contract, error recovery, focus behavior and the exact runtime checks still needed.
example: A flow declares idle, loading, success and error, but only connects idle to loading and loading to success; empty is required.
improvement: An original task-specific procedure paired with a bounded executable tool, discriminating public exercises and explicit outcome limits.

depth.domain_method: Represent the interface as a deterministic declared state graph and keep that specification separate from runtime evidence. Validate state identities and transition endpoints, reject conflicting transitions for the same state/event, and traverse from the initial state. Report required states that are missing, declared states that are unreachable, and reachable nonterminal dead ends. The graph helps expose forgotten loading/error/empty behavior; actual navigation, keyboard, persistence and visual continuity still require a rendered product test.
depth.output_contract: Return reachable and unreachable states, missing required states, nonterminal dead ends and a scoped declared-graph status. browser_tested is always false. A complete design handoff includes each state purpose, visible feedback, event contract, error recovery, focus behavior and the exact runtime checks still needed.

decisions.when: A required empty or error state is absent.
decisions.do: Report the missing state and define its content, available actions and recovery before claiming complete coverage.
decisions.avoid: Do not treat a happy-path success screen as sufficient for every outcome.

decisions.when: A declared state has no path from the initial state.
decisions.do: Inspect whether a transition is missing or the state is obsolete and reconcile the specification.
decisions.avoid: Do not count an unreachable screen as covered simply because it is named.

decisions.when: A reachable nonterminal state has no outgoing transition.
decisions.do: Identify the blocked user journey and add a deliberate recovery or terminal classification.
decisions.avoid: Do not let users become stuck without an intentional completion boundary.

decisions.when: The same state and event lead to two targets.
decisions.do: Reject the ambiguity and model the guard condition explicitly before implementation.
decisions.avoid: Do not let list order decide user-visible behavior.

decisions.when: Every declared state and transition is consistent.
decisions.do: Report a complete declared graph while retaining browser and accessibility checks as separate work.
decisions.avoid: Do not translate graph consistency into a claim of an executed end-to-end test.

failure_modes.symptom: A failed submission leaves the interface permanently loading.
failure_modes.cause: The implementation or specification omitted a failure transition and recovery action.
failure_modes.repair: Add the error path and verify preserved input and a usable retry boundary.
failure_modes.recheck: The error state is reachable and the user has an explicit recovery transition.

failure_modes.symptom: Designers and developers disagree about the same button event.
failure_modes.cause: The transition contract contains multiple targets without modeled guards.
failure_modes.repair: Name distinct events or guard outcomes and make the state/event mapping deterministic.
failure_modes.recheck: Each declared state/event pair has one unambiguous transition.

failure_modes.symptom: A complete diagram still produces a broken keyboard flow.
failure_modes.cause: Specification coverage was mistaken for runtime and accessibility evidence.
failure_modes.repair: Run the actual keyboard/focus sequence and capture the failing rendered state.
failure_modes.recheck: The final report keeps declared graph checks and observed browser checks separately labeled.

worked_example.method: Traverse from idle and compare the declared set with the required checklist.
worked_example.result: The report identifies missing empty and unreachable error; browser_tested remains false.

additional_examples.input: Add failure from loading to error and retry from error to idle, with success as a terminal state.
additional_examples.method: Check that every required state is reachable and every reachable nonterminal has a way forward.
additional_examples.result: The declared graph is complete, but real rendering, keyboard behavior and actual network failure still need execution evidence.
